
with:

```python
def _inside_dashboard(context):
    """Whether this page draws the dashboard's menu (spec 4.4): a signed-in visitor, on an address whose URL name registry.DASHBOARD_SECTIONS lists,
    on a page that has not asked for the ordinary menu. A page asks with `plain_menu`: the error pages and the throttled page do, since they carry
    nothing that belongs to a person and no token (AGENTS.md, "Error pages"), whichever address they are drawn for. A page drawn with no request
    (the miss page of /a/<token>) is never inside."""
    request = context.get("request")
    user = getattr(request, "user", None)
    match = getattr(request, "resolver_match", None)
    return bool(
        user is not None and user.is_authenticated
        and getattr(match, "url_name", None) in registry.DASHBOARD_SECTIONS
        and not context.get("plain_menu")
    )


@register.simple_tag(takes_context=True)
def shell_menu(context):
    """The menu's groups for this request: Sign in or Dashboard, and the current page marked; inside the dashboard, its sections instead (see _inside_dashboard)."""
    request = context.get("request")
    user = getattr(request, "user", None)
    match = getattr(request, "resolver_match", None)
    return registry.menu_groups(
        signed_in=bool(user is not None and user.is_authenticated),
        current=getattr(match, "url_name", None),
        inside_dashboard=_inside_dashboard(context),
    )


@register.simple_tag(takes_context=True)
def shell_sign_out(context):
    """The CSRF token for the Sign out button that ends group 2 of the menu inside the dashboard, and an empty string on every other page. It is asked
    for only inside the dashboard, so that no other page sets the CSRF cookie or carries a token: the public pages, the throttled page and the miss
    page of /a/<token> stay as they are (shell.html passes it to the menu as sign_out)."""
    return get_token(context["request"]) if _inside_dashboard(context) else ""
```

```python
"""The app layout and its family (spec 4.8, 6.2): the shell's entry for a section, the public head a section does not print, the body's family attributes and the faces."""
import re
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest import mock

from django.template.loader import render_to_string
from django.test import TestCase

from dashboard.tests_app import SECTIONS, headings, signed_in_client
from pages import registry
from pages.context_processors import shell_page
from pages.tests_head import request_for

APP_PATHS = "/app/ /app/files/ /app/keys/ /app/apps/ /app/billing/"
APP_FACES = "italic 300 1em Cormorant Garamond|1em Newsreader"
PUBLIC_HEAD = ('rel="canonical"', 'property="og:', 'name="twitter:card"', "application/ld+json", 'rel="alternate"', 'name="description"', "data-page-meta")


def head_and_body_tag(html):
    return html[:html.index("</head>")], re.search(r"<body[^>]*>", html).group(0)


class AppEntryTests(TestCase):
    longMessage = False

    def test_each_section_has_an_entry_in_the_app_layout_with_its_title_and_no_public_address(self):
        for name, address, label in SECTIONS:
            with self.subTest(section=name):
                entry = shell_page(request_for(address))["shell_page"]
                self.assertTrue(entry, f"backend/pages/context_processors.py: shell_page gives {name} an entry, or it joins no family")
                self.assertEqual(entry["title"], f"{label} | Veilfile")
                self.assertEqual(entry["layout"], "app")
                self.assertEqual(entry["layout_paths"], APP_PATHS, "backend/pages/registry.py: layout_paths('app') is the five sections' addresses, in menu order")
                self.assertEqual((entry["canonical"], entry["description"], entry["image"], entry["article"]), ("", "", "", None),
                                 "backend/pages/context_processors.py: a dashboard section has no canonical address, description or preview image")

    def test_the_entry_is_built_when_read_and_asks_for_no_static_file(self):
        request = request_for("/app/files/")
        with mock.patch("pages.context_processors.static", side_effect=ValueError("Missing staticfiles manifest entry")):
            entry = shell_page(request)["shell_page"]
            self.assertEqual(entry["title"], "Files | Veilfile", "backend/pages/context_processors.py: a dashboard entry needs no preview image, so no manifest entry")

    def test_a_dashboard_name_that_is_not_a_section_has_no_entry(self):
        # A confirmation page is listed in DASHBOARD_SECTIONS (it marks its section in the menu) but is a page of its own: it loads as an ordinary page.
        request = request_for("/app/")
        request.resolver_match = SimpleNamespace(url_name="app-file-revoke", kwargs={})
        with mock.patch.dict(registry.DASHBOARD_SECTIONS, {"app-file-revoke": "app-files"}):
            self.assertEqual(shell_page(request), {"shell_page": None}, "backend/pages/registry.py: dashboard_section() finds only the five sections of DASHBOARD_MENU")
        self.assertFalse(shell_page(request_for("/app/components/"))["shell_page"])

    def test_the_family_is_the_five_sections_and_no_chapter_or_reading_page(self):
        self.assertEqual(" ".join(registry.layout_paths("app")), APP_PATHS)
        for layout in ("chapter", "reading"):
            self.assertFalse(set(registry.layout_paths("app")) & set(registry.layout_paths(layout)))


class AppHeadTests(TestCase):
    longMessage = False

    def setUp(self):

    def test_a_section_prints_none_of_the_public_head(self):

                for needle in PUBLIC_HEAD:
                    self.assertNotIn(needle, head, f"backend/templates/shell.html: {address} is not a public page, so its head prints no {needle}; the public head is printed only when shell_page.canonical is set")

    def test_it_is_kept_out_of_search_by_a_tag_as_well_as_the_header(self):
        for _, address, _ in SECTIONS:
            with self.subTest(address=address):
                head, _ = head_and_body_tag(self.client.get(address).content.decode())
                self.assertIn('<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">', head, "backend/templates/layouts/app.html: the meta block carries the noindex tag")

    def test_the_body_names_the_family_its_paths_and_its_faces(self):
        for _, address, _ in SECTIONS:
            with self.subTest(address=address):
                _, body = head_and_body_tag(self.client.get(address).content.decode())
                self.assertEqual(body, f'<body class="layout-app" data-veil-src="/static/js/veil.js" data-layout="app" data-layout-paths="{APP_PATHS}" data-faces="{APP_FACES}">',
                                 "backend/templates/shell.html: data-layout, data-layout-paths and data-faces come from shell_page.layout; layouts/app.html gives the body class")

    def test_it_preloads_the_display_face_for_its_title_and_the_two_it_always_does(self):
        html = self.client.get("/app/").content.decode()
        self.assertEqual(set(re.findall(r'<link rel="preload" href="/static/([^"]+\.woff2)" as="font"', html)),
                         {"fonts/cormorant-garamond/italic-300-latin.woff2", "fonts/newsreader/normal-400-500-latin.woff2", "fonts/ibm-plex-mono/normal-400-latin.woff2"},
                         "backend/templates/layouts/app.html preloads italic 300 (the title); italic 400 is not set anywhere in the dashboard")

    def test_an_entry_with_a_layout_and_no_canonical_address_prints_no_empty_one(self):
        # The trap in a half-made entry: shell.html resolves a missing key to an empty string, so keyed on the entry itself it would print
        # <link rel="canonical" href=""> and blank Open Graph tags.
        request = request_for("/app/")
        entry = {"title": "Anything | Veilfile", "layout": "app", "layout_paths": "/app/"}
        head, body = head_and_body_tag(render_to_string("shell.html", {"shell_page": entry}, request=request))
        self.assertIn("<title>Anything | Veilfile</title>", head)
        for needle in PUBLIC_HEAD:
            self.assertNotIn(needle, head, f"backend/templates/shell.html: print {needle} only when shell_page.canonical is set")
        self.assertIn('data-layout="app"', body, "the family comes from shell_page.layout whatever the head prints")

    def test_a_public_page_still_prints_its_whole_head(self):
        head, body = head_and_body_tag(self.client.get("/about/").content.decode())
        for needle in PUBLIC_HEAD:
            self.assertIn(needle, head)
        self.assertNotIn(APP_FACES, body)
```

Create `backend/dashboard/tests_app_css.py`:

```python
"""The dashboard's CSS (spec 4.8, 4.10): the column, its type, the rows that stack when the column is narrow, and the markup that pattern needs."""
import re
from html.parser import HTMLParser
from pathlib import Path

from django.conf import settings
from django.test import SimpleTestCase

STATIC = Path(settings.BASE_DIR) / "static"
TEMPLATES = Path(settings.BASE_DIR) / "templates"


class RowsMarkup(HTMLParser):
    """Reads a template's text for the rows pattern (base.css): every table is table.rows with a name, every header cell has scope="col", every td has a data-label."""

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.problems, self.tables, self.inside, self.named = [], 0, False, False

    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        found = dict(attrs)
        if tag == "table":
            if "rows" not in (found.get("class") or "").split():
                self.problems.append("a <table> that is not class=\"rows\"")
                return
            self.tables, self.inside, self.named = self.tables + 1, True, bool(found.get("aria-label"))
        elif self.inside and tag == "caption":
            self.named = True
        elif self.inside and tag == "th" and found.get("scope") != "col":
            self.problems.append("a <th> without scope=\"col\"")
        elif self.inside and tag == "td" and not found.get("data-label"):
            self.problems.append("a <td> without a data-label")

    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        if tag == "table" and self.inside:
            self.inside = False
            if not self.named:
                self.problems.append("a table.rows with no <caption> and no aria-label")


def rows_problems(text):
    parser = RowsMarkup()
    parser.feed(text)
    return parser.problems


class AppCssTests(SimpleTestCase):
    longMessage = False

    def setUp(self):
        self.base = re.sub(r"/\*.*?\*/", "", (STATIC / "css" / "base.css").read_text(encoding="utf-8"), flags=re.S)
        self.tokens = (STATIC / "css" / "tokens.css").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    def rule(self, selector):
        """The declarations of the first rule whose selector is exactly `selector` (as written, spaces folded)."""
        for found, body in re.findall(r"([^{}]+)\{([^{}]*)\}", self.base):
            if " ".join(found.split()) == selector:
                return " ".join(body.split())
        self.fail(f"backend/static/css/base.css: no rule for {selector}")

    def test_the_column_starts_at_the_top_scrolls_with_the_page_and_is_a_container(self):
        self.assertIn("display: grid;", self.rule(".layout-app .shell-main"))
        self.assertIn("align-content: start;", self.rule(".layout-app .shell-main"))
        column = self.rule(".app")
        for declaration in ("container: app / inline-size;", "width: 100%;", "min-width: 0;", "max-width: var(--app-measure);", "overflow-wrap: anywhere;"):
            self.assertIn(declaration, column, f"backend/static/css/base.css: .app needs {declaration}")
        self.assertIn("--app-measure: 60rem;", self.tokens, "backend/static/css/tokens.css: --app-measure is the dashboard's column")

    def test_the_title_is_a_chapters_title_and_the_smaller_headings_are_mono_labels(self):
        self.assertIn("font-style: italic; font-weight: 300;", self.rule(".app :where(h1)"))
        label = self.rule(".app :where(h2, h3, dt, legend, caption)")
        for declaration in ("font-family: var(--font-mono);", "text-transform: uppercase;", "color: var(--muted);"):
            self.assertIn(declaration, label)

    def test_no_dashboard_rule_sets_text_in_the_heading_face_the_layout_does_not_name(self):
        # data-faces (APP_FACES) names italic 300 and Newsreader: a change in place loads those before it swaps. Italic 400 (--font-heading) is not named,
        # so nothing in the dashboard may be set in it; if a section needs it, name it in templates/shell.html and tests_faces.LAYOUT_FACES together.
        read = 0
        for selector, body in re.findall(r"([^{}]+)\{([^{}]*)\}", self.base):
            if re.search(r"\.(app|rows|layout-app)\b", selector):
                read += 1
                self.assertNotIn("--font-heading", body, f"backend/static/css/base.css: {' '.join(selector.split())} sets text in --font-heading, which the app layout's data-faces does not name")
        self.assertGreater(read, 20, "backend/dashboard/tests_app_css.py: this check read no dashboard rules; .app, .rows and .layout-app are in backend/static/css/base.css")

    def test_link_hover_waits_for_a_pointer_that_can_hover(self):
        self.assertRegex(self.base, r"@media not all and \(pointer: coarse\) \{\s*\.app :is\(p, li, dd, \.notice\) a:not\(\.interactive, \.label\):hover \{",
                         "backend/static/css/base.css: gate the dashboard link hover on `not all and (pointer: coarse)`, never (hover: hover): CI's Chromium reports hover: none")

    def test_rows_are_a_table_that_stacks_when_the_column_is_narrow_not_the_window(self):
        stacked = re.search(r"@container app \(max-width: 39\.99rem\) \{(.*?)\n\}", self.base, flags=re.S)
        self.assertTrue(stacked, "backend/static/css/base.css: rows stack in @container app (max-width: 39.99rem), a query on the column: between the corners it is 394px at 1024 and 624px at 1280")
        block = " ".join(stacked.group(1).split())
        for needle in (".rows thead { position: absolute;", "clip-path: inset(50%);", ".rows, .rows tbody, .rows tr, .rows td { display: block; }",
                       ".rows caption { display: block; }", ".rows td::before { content: attr(data-label); display: block;", ".rows td:empty { display: none; }"):
            self.assertIn(needle, block, f"backend/static/css/base.css: the stacked rows need {needle}")
        windows = re.findall(r"@media[^{]*\{(?:[^{}]*\{[^{}]*\})*[^{}]*\}", self.base)
        self.assertEqual([window[:80] for window in windows if ".rows" in window], [], "backend/static/css/base.css: .rows follows its column (@container), never the window (@media)")

    def test_the_table_wraps_a_name_anywhere_and_every_other_cell_at_its_spaces(self):
        self.assertIn("overflow-wrap: normal;", self.rule(".rows :where(th, td)"))
        self.assertIn("overflow-wrap: anywhere;", self.rule(".rows :where(td:first-child, td[data-wrap])"))


class RowsMarkupTests(SimpleTestCase):
    longMessage = False

    def test_every_table_in_a_dashboard_template_follows_the_rows_pattern(self):
        for path in sorted((TEMPLATES / "dashboard").rglob("*.html")):
            with self.subTest(template=path.name):
                self.assertEqual(rows_problems(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")), [],
                                 f"backend/templates/dashboard/{path.name}: a table is <table class=\"rows\"> with a <caption> (or an aria-label), <th scope=\"col\"> headers and a "
                                 "data-label on every <td>, so that it stacks into rows that keep each value's label on a phone (backend/static/css/base.css, spec 4.10)")

    def test_the_check_finds_what_it_names(self):
        good = ('<table class="rows"><caption>Files</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">Name</th></tr></thead>'
                '<tbody><tr><td data-label="Name">a</td></tr></tbody></table>')
        self.assertEqual(rows_problems(good), [], "backend/dashboard/tests_app_css.py: rows_problems() must accept the pattern")
        self.assertEqual(rows_problems(good.replace(' class="rows"', ' class="plain"')), ['a <table> that is not class="rows"'])
        self.assertEqual(rows_problems(good.replace("<caption>Files</caption>", "")), ["a table.rows with no <caption> and no aria-label"])
        self.assertEqual(rows_problems(good.replace("<caption>Files</caption>", "").replace('class="rows"', 'class="rows" aria-label="Files"')), [])
        self.assertEqual(rows_problems(good.replace('<th scope="col">', "<th>")), ['a <th> without scope="col"'])
        self.assertEqual(rows_problems(good.replace(' data-label="Name"', "")), ["a <td> without a data-label"])
```

- [ ] **Step 12: The dashboard's CSS and its measure**

`--app-measure` is a size token, so it needs no `@property` rule (only colours do). The block goes in `base.css` with the rules every page has, before the main action's rules: an in-place change brings no stylesheet with it, so a section's CSS cannot live in a page sheet. It comes before `.notice`, which therefore keeps the margin it has on a form page.

In `backend/static/css/tokens.css`, replace this exact text:

```css

```

with:

```css
  --form-measure: 26rem; /* a form page's column (layout-form, base.css): about fifty characters of Newsreader */
  --app-measure: 60rem; /* the dashboard's column at most (layout-app, base.css): the room between the corners is narrower than this until the window is about 1650px wide */
```

In `backend/static/css/base.css`, replace this exact text (it occurs once: the first line of the main action's comment):

```css
/* The main action (the owner's choice): a mono label in a 1px hairline box on --box, one to a form. Its box stays --hair: a button is
```

with:

```css
/* The dashboard (spec 4.8): its five sections, on layouts/app.html. One column that starts at the top and scrolls with the page, as the reading column
   does, centred between the corners and no wider than --app-measure. The sections are a family of their own (data-layout="app"), so moving between them
   changes in place, and an in-place change brings no stylesheet with it: everything a section needs is here, with the rules every page has. As in the
   reading and form columns the bare elements are styled where they stand, `.app :where(...)` weighing one class and no element, so a component's own
   class overrides them by source order. A long name, address or app name wraps, anywhere, so the page never scrolls sideways at 320; min-width: 0 lets
   the column be narrower than its widest content. Newsreader has no face heavier than 500 (strong, below), so nothing is drawn in a synthetic bold.
   The column is a container (named app): the rows below ask how wide it is, not how wide the window is, because between the corners it is only 394px at
   1024 and 624px at 1280. Text here is set in the title's face (italic 300), Newsreader and the mono labels, which is what the layout's data-faces names. */
.layout-app .shell-main {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr);
  justify-items: center;
  align-content: start;
}

.app {
  container: app / inline-size;
  width: 100%;
  min-width: 0;
  max-width: var(--app-measure);
  font-variant-numeric: lining-nums;
  font-synthesis-weight: none;
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}

/* The title is a chapter's title (.chapter__title): the display face, italic 300. */
.app :where(h1) {
  margin: 0 0 var(--space-4);
  font-family: var(--font-display);
  font-style: italic;
  font-weight: 300;
  font-size: var(--title-size);
  line-height: 1.15;
  text-wrap: balance;
}

/* A smaller heading, a term in a list of facts, a fieldset's legend and a table's caption are labels: mono, uppercase, muted. */
.app :where(h2, h3, dt, legend, caption) {
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: var(--label-size);
  font-weight: 400;
  letter-spacing: var(--label-tracking);
  line-height: 1.4;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--muted);
}

.app :where(h2, h3) {
  margin: var(--space-4) 0 var(--space-2);
}

.app :where(dt) {
  margin: var(--space-2) 0 0;
}

.app :where(dd) {
  margin: 0;
}

/* Not the visually hidden ones: their margin is what clips them. */
.app :where(p:not(.visually-hidden), ul, ol, dl) {
  margin: 0 0 var(--space-3);
}

.app :where(ul, ol) {
  padding: 0 0 0 1.8em; /* room for the markers, which are the browser's */
}

.app :where(li) {
  margin: 0 0 var(--space-1);
}

.app :where(strong, b) {
  font-weight: 500; /* the heaviest face Newsreader has */
}

.app :where(code) {
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: .8em;
}

/* min-width: 0, or a fieldset (whose default is its widest content) holds the page wider than a phone. */
.app :where(fieldset) {
  min-width: 0;
  margin: 0 0 var(--space-4);
  padding: 0;
  border: 0;
}

.app :where(legend) {
  padding: 0 0 var(--space-2);
}

/* A part of a section's page (the plan, the meters, the list, the form): a <section> with its own label. After the margins above, so the first thing in
   one starts at its top. */
.app :where(section) {
  margin: var(--space-5) 0 0;
}

.app :where(section > :first-child) {
  margin-top: 0;
}

/* Inline links in the dashboard's words (a notice, a line under a label): the dotted underline that gives way to the flat fill, as on a form page. veil.js
   washes the chapters' and the reading column's prose links and not these. A labelled link (.label) is not one: it is an action. */
.app :is(p, li, dd, .notice) a:not(.interactive, .label) {
  text-decoration: underline dotted var(--muted);
  text-decoration-thickness: 1px;
  text-underline-offset: .22em;
  transition: background-color var(--fill-fade) ease, text-decoration-color var(--fill-fade) ease;
}

.app :is(p, li, dd, .notice) a:not(.interactive, .label):focus-visible {
  background-color: var(--fill);
  text-decoration-color: transparent;
}

@media not all and (pointer: coarse) {
  .app :is(p, li, dd, .notice) a:not(.interactive, .label):hover {
    background-color: var(--fill);
    text-decoration-color: transparent;
  }
}

@media (pointer: coarse) {
  .app :is(p, li, dd, .notice) a:not(.interactive, .label):active {
    background-color: var(--fill);
    text-decoration-color: transparent;
  }
}

/* Rows (spec 4.8, 4.10): the dashboard's lists of files, keys and connected apps, as <table class="rows"> with a <caption>, `th scope="col"` headers and a
   `data-label` on every td (the name of its column). A table where the column is wide enough to hold one; where it is not, stacked rows: the header row goes
   (hidden from sight, not from screen readers), each row is a block, and each cell is led by its column's name from data-label, so every value keeps its label.
   The first column holds the name a person gave (a file, a key, an app) and breaks anywhere; so does a cell marked data-wrap. Every other cell breaks at its
   spaces only, so a date and a size stay whole whatever a name does to the columns. A cell with nothing in it is not drawn when stacked. */
.rows {
  width: 100%;
  border-collapse: collapse;
  font-size: .9em;
}

.rows caption {
  padding: 0 0 var(--space-2);
  text-align: left;
}

.rows :where(th, td) {
  padding: var(--space-2) var(--space-3) var(--space-2) 0;
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--hair);
  text-align: left;
  vertical-align: top;
  overflow-wrap: normal;
}

.rows :where(td:first-child, td[data-wrap]) {
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}

.rows th,
.rows td::before {
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: var(--label-size);
  font-weight: 400;
  letter-spacing: var(--label-tracking);
  line-height: 1.4;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--muted);
}

@container app (max-width: 39.99rem) {
  .rows thead {
    position: absolute;
    width: 1px;
    height: 1px;
    margin: -1px;
    overflow: hidden;
    clip-path: inset(50%);
    white-space: nowrap;
  }

  .rows,
  .rows tbody,
  .rows tr,
  .rows td {
    display: block;
  }

  .rows caption {
    display: block;
  }

  .rows tbody tr:first-child {
    border-top: 1px solid var(--hair);
  }

  .rows tr {
    padding: var(--space-3) 0 var(--space-2);
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--hair);
  }

  .rows td {
    padding: 0 0 var(--space-2);
    border: 0;
    overflow-wrap: anywhere;
  }

  .rows td::before {
    content: attr(data-label);
    display: block;
    margin: 0 0 var(--space-1);
  }

  .rows td:empty {
    display: none;
  }
}

/* The main action (the owner's choice): a mono label in a 1px hairline box on --box, one to a form. Its box stays --hair: a button is
```

```python
"""static/js/behaviors/local-time.js (spec 4.8): the server's UTC text becomes the visitor's own time. The script is read here, not run (these tests have no browser);
the dashboard's browser checks run it."""
import re
from pathlib import Path

from django.conf import settings
from django.test import SimpleTestCase

from dashboard.tests_filters import render

JS = Path(settings.BASE_DIR) / "static" / "js"


class LocalTimeScriptTests(SimpleTestCase):
    """static/js/behaviors/local-time.js (spec 4.8): the server's UTC text becomes the visitor's own time. The script is read here, not run (no browser in
    these tests); the browser checks of the dashboard run it."""
    longMessage = False
    FILE = "backend/static/js/behaviors/local-time.js"

    def setUp(self):
        self.script = (JS / "behaviors" / "local-time.js").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    def test_it_finds_the_elements_utc_time_writes_and_reads_the_machine_readable_time(self):
        html = render("{{ value|utc_time }}", value="2026-10-22T13:58:55+00:00")
        self.assertIn(" data-local>", html)
        self.assertIn('document.querySelectorAll("time[data-local]")', self.script, f"{self.FILE}: it rewrites every <time data-local>, the markup utc_time writes")
        self.assertIn("new Date(time.dateTime)", self.script, f"{self.FILE}: it reads the datetime attribute, never the UTC text")

    def test_it_formats_in_the_visitors_own_zone_and_names_it(self):
        self.assertIn('new Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, { year: "numeric", month: "short", day: "numeric", hour: "numeric", minute: "2-digit", timeZoneName: "short" })', self.script,
                      f"{self.FILE}: Intl.DateTimeFormat in the visitor's locale: the date, the time to the minute and the zone's short name (timeZoneName: \"short\")")
        options = re.search(r"new Intl\.DateTimeFormat\(undefined, \{(.*?)\}\)", self.script, re.S)
        self.assertTrue(options, f"{self.FILE}: the formatter's options are an object literal")
        self.assertEqual(sorted(re.findall(r"(\w+)\s*:", options.group(1))), ["day", "hour", "minute", "month", "timeZoneName", "year"],
                         f"{self.FILE}: exactly these options: no dateStyle or timeStyle (they cannot be combined with timeZoneName) and no timeZone, which would pin one zone for every visitor")
        self.assertNotRegex(self.script, r"\btimeZone\s*:", f"{self.FILE}: no timeZone option: the zone is the visitor's own (timeZoneName only says which it is)")

    def test_a_time_it_cannot_read_keeps_its_utc_text_and_no_title_is_added(self):
        self.assertIn("if (!Number.isNaN(moment.getTime())) time.textContent = format.format(moment);", self.script,
                      f"{self.FILE}: a time that does not parse keeps the text the server wrote")
        self.assertNotIn("title", self.script.lower(), f"{self.FILE}: no title attribute; a tooltip is not read on a phone or by keyboard, and the UTC text is for visitors with no script")

    def test_it_runs_on_load_and_after_each_change_in_place(self):
        self.assertIn("\nlocalTimes();\n", self.script, f"{self.FILE}: run once on load (a module runs after the page is parsed)")
        self.assertIn('document.addEventListener("veilfile:swapped", localTimes);', self.script, f"{self.FILE}: run after each change in place, delegated from the document")
        self.assertIn('new CustomEvent("veilfile:swapped")', (JS / "shell.js").read_text(encoding="utf-8"), "backend/static/js/shell.js fires veilfile:swapped after a swap")
```

- [ ] **Step 14: The local-time behaviour**

A module that runs once the page is parsed and again after each swap. A `<time>` that has no `datetime`, or one that does not parse, keeps what the server wrote.

Create `backend/static/js/behaviors/local-time.js`:

```javascript
// Local time (spec 4.8): the server writes each time in UTC inside <time datetime data-local>; this writes it again in the visitor's own zone, on load
// and after each change in place. With no script, or a time it cannot read, the UTC text stays. AGENTS.md, "How shell.js works", "Behaviours".
const format = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, { year: "numeric", month: "short", day: "numeric", hour: "numeric", minute: "2-digit", timeZoneName: "short" });

function localTimes() {
  for (const time of document.querySelectorAll("time[data-local]")) {
    const moment = new Date(time.dateTime);
    if (!Number.isNaN(moment.getTime())) time.textContent = format.format(moment);
  }
}

localTimes();
document.addEventListener("veilfile:swapped", localTimes);
```

### Task 3: Overview, the meter and the password pages

Overview (`/app/`) becomes the first page of the dashboard: what the account has used, what it is over, and the account itself. It keeps the React dashboard's sentences where they still apply (the four `?billing=` notices, the verify-your-email prompt, the over-limit lines) and shows the figures as meters. This task adds the one component the dashboard needs for that, `meter`, and moves `/accounts/password_change/` and the page it ends on from the Django admin's skin onto the form layout, because Overview now links to them.

The figures come from the account functions the JSON endpoints answer with (Task 1), so Overview and `/api/v1/usage/` cannot disagree. The words are the templates'. The two reads that feed the page are separate: a read that fails leaves out its own part, says so in one sentence and takes nothing else with it.

**What a visitor sees change** (from the React dashboard's Usage section and banners; Task 2 moved the page itself):
- `used / cap` becomes `used of cap` with a hairline bar under it, and the storage figures are in GB (React printed `1024.0 MB` for a gigabyte). The bar stays full past the cap and the figure says `Over the limit` in words.
- `Link TTL` becomes `Links last up to`, and the `plan: free` badge becomes `You are on the Free plan.` with a link to Billing.
- `Try again from Billing below.` and `Switch plans or manage billing below.` no longer say below: Billing is another page, so they link to it.
- The over-limit lines gain a fourth line. A downgrade can leave the month's uploads over the new cap, which the billing status has no flag for, and the meter alone would not put that first.
- The account gains a line: the address, whether it is verified, and `Change email` and `Change password` (nothing linked to the password page before).
- `/accounts/password_change/` and `/accounts/password_change/done/` are pages of the site: the shell, one `h1`, labelled fields with their errors tied to them, a sentence that says what a change does.

Every other sentence is React's, word for word, and the tests pin each.

**Decisions** (the skeleton leaves them to this task):

- **The meter is `role="meter"` on a `div`, over an SVG; not `<meter>`, not `role="progressbar"`.**
  - *Why not `progressbar`.* It says a task is under way, and assistive technology announces it so. A quota is not that; `meter` is ARIA's name for a scalar against a known range, which is what `<meter>` means too.
  - *Why not `<meter>`.* A page may not carry an inline style (`pages.tests_site_rules`), so the fill's width has to come from an attribute. The native element draws its fill from `value`, but only through `::-webkit-meter-*` and `::-moz-meter-bar` rules that differ by engine, and nothing in the browser checks looks at how it is drawn. An SVG whose `rect` has a `width` attribute draws the same everywhere, and the box round it is a border, which a forced-colours screen keeps.
  - *What it costs.* The role is not native. The numbers are always in the text above the bar, and the bar is named by the label (`aria-labelledby`) and described by the figures (`aria-describedby`), so an engine that ignores the role loses nothing. `aria-valuenow` cannot pass `aria-valuemax`, so past the cap it is the cap and the description carries the true figure.
  - The SVG's `viewBox` is 1000 wide whatever the limit, and the fill is the figure in thousandths of it (`{% widthratio %}`): a storage cap in bytes (26843545600) never reaches a coordinate.
- **The month is the UTC month, and the page says so.** One line under the uploads bar: `Counted by calendar month, in UTC.` The counter's month is `timezone.now().strftime("%Y-%m")` (`services._current_month`, `views._current_month`), so a visitor in New York sees it turn over at 8 pm on the last evening, and spec 5 asks that a fact on the page match its source. It is a note under the bar and not in the label, so the label stays React's words.
- **The over-limit lines are one include, `dashboard/over_limits.html`, made here and used by Billing (Task 6) too.** Overview comes first in the order of tasks, so this task makes the include and owns the file: Task 6 only includes it (`{% include "dashboard/over_limits.html" with status=status only %}`) and does not create it. Its inputs are the billing status (`status`) and, optionally, the usage (`usage`). The sentences are in the template, with the figures as variables, so the voice pass edits one file; no Python formats a size.
- **The uploads line is new.** `over_plan_limits` has `keys`, `storage` and `ttl` and no uploads flag, but a downgrade (Team to Free with 500 uploads this month) leaves `uploads_used` above `uploads_cap`, and new uploads are then refused (`monthly_cap_reached`, `services.py`) until the month turns over. Spec 4.8 says anything over a limit is shown first, so the include adds one line when `usage.uploads_used > usage.uploads_cap`, from the usage alone. It is worded like the storage line: `Existing links keep working, but new uploads are refused until the next month begins (UTC).`
- **A read that fails is left out, logged and said in one sentence; the page is never a 500 for it.** `overview_page.read` calls an account function and answers its body, or `None` when it raised or answered other than 200. It catches `Exception` on purpose: `UsageView` indexes `PLANS[workspace.plan]` with no fallback (Task 1 moves its body into `usage()` unchanged), so an unknown plan name is a `KeyError`, and the first page after sign in must not die of it. The traceback goes to the log (`logger.exception`); the page prints no detail, and a test holds that.
  - Usage down: the Usage section says `Usage could not be loaded just now. Reload the page to try again.`; the limit lines, the plan (from the status) and the account still show.
  - Status down: a notice says `Plan limits could not be checked just now. Reload the page to check again.` where the limit lines would be; the meters, the plan (from usage), the account and, from usage alone, the uploads line still show.
- **Customer wording only (ruling R1).** Every sentence Overview shows, the four `?billing=` notices included, is React's customer wording or this task's own: none names Stripe, an error code or an instance, and a failed read never prints Stripe's message or any detail (a 502 `stripe_error` or a 503 `billing_not_configured` from the status shows the one sentence `Plan limits could not be checked just now. Reload the page to check again.`). `test_no_state_of_the_page_shows_the_operators_words` holds it for every notice and each kind of failed read. Overview gives no reference code: it is not a refusal of an action, the sentence asks for a reload, and the log line (`dashboard: the billing status answered 502 ...`) holds the detail.
- **The account line does not use the usage read.** The address and its state are `user.email` and `is_email_verified(user)`, the function the usage body uses, so a usage that fails does not take the verify prompt or the account with it.
- **The prompt names the address the link went to.** React printed `usage.email`, the account address. After a change of address (`drop_core.views.email_verification`) `user.email` stays the old one until the new one is verified, while the link went to the one on the `EmailVerification` row, so the prompt names that. With no row it keeps React's other sentence, `Add an email address to your account.`
- **The notices' plan is checked against `plans.PLANS`, and only its name is printed.** `?plan=` counts when it is a key of `PLANS` with a price above 0 (`free` is never bought), and the page prints `plan.title()` of that key, as `pages/plan_cards.py` writes the names. A test adds a plan to `PLANS` and watches the notice follow, so the check cannot be a list typed in the view.
- **The sentences that said `below`.** `Try again from Billing below.` becomes `Try again from Billing.` and `Switch plans or manage billing below.` becomes a link, `Switch plans or manage billing.` The `success` notice keeps `below`: the plan it speaks of is further down this page.
- **Password pages: no autofocus of their own, not in the dashboard menu.**
  - Three fields, so by AGENTS.md ("none on a page of several fields") no field takes focus on a clean page, and the first field in error takes it after a failed submit (`{% focus_field %}` with no default, `{% focus_summary %}` for the form's own errors, as the reset form has them).

The way back is `Back to dashboard` (the verify page's words), and the done page's main action is `Go to dashboard`.

API keys keep working.`, is true and a test holds each part: `PasswordChangeView` calls `update_session_auth_hash` (other sessions die), `RevokingPasswordChangeView.form_valid` revokes the OAuth grants, and `tests_fix_auth.PasswordChangeRevokesOAuthTests` pins that API keys survive.

Markup hooks that later tasks and the browser checks use: `.meters` (the list), `.meter`, `.meter--over`, `.meter__label`, `.meter__figures`, `.meter__flag`, `.meter__bar` with `role="meter"`, `.meter__fill`, `.meter__note`.

Task 6 includes it with `{% include "dashboard/over_limits.html" with status=status only %}` and does not make it again; its tests read the visible text of this file (the page without `usage` simply has no uploads line).

  - Tests: `pages.tests_meter` (23), `dashboard.tests_overview` (38), `drop_core.tests_password_change_pages` (20).

Facts the steps rely on (all checked in the code):
1. **Django's password change views use these template names, and the project has none of its own.** `PasswordChangeView` renders `registration/password_change_form.html` with `form` (`old_password`, `new_password1`, `new_password2`) and ends on `password_change_done`, a `PasswordChangeDoneView` that renders `registration/password_change_done.html`. Both need a session. With no template in `backend/templates/registration/`, Django finds the admin's (`Old password:`, the admin's header), which is why nothing linked to them.
2. **The errors land where the reset form's do.** A wrong old password is on `old_password` ("Your old password was entered incorrectly. Please enter it again."). The mismatch and the validators' errors are on `new_password2`. `new_password1` only carries "This field is required."
3. **A successful change keeps the session that made it and ends the others** (`update_session_auth_hash` cycles the key and stores the new hash; another session's stored hash no longer matches). `RevokingPasswordChangeView.form_valid` then revokes the OAuth grants; API keys are left alone.
4. **`{% if %}` swallows an error in a comparison.** `{% if usage.uploads_used > usage.uploads_cap %}` is false when `usage` is `None`, and `"keys" in status.over_plan_limits` is false when `status` is. A filter's argument is not so forgiving: `{{ status.plan|default:usage.plan }}` raises `VariableDoesNotExist` when `usage` is `None`, so the include uses `{% if %}` and `{% else %}`.
5. **`{% load %}` may sit on the third line of a component.** `pages.tests_site_rules` holds a component's first two lines to being its two comments, nothing more.
6. **The shell's template rules apply to every template that extends a layout** (`pages.tests_site_rules`, `pages.tests_content`): no `style=`, components included with `only`, no `<header>` or `<footer>`, every character in all three fonts (these templates are ASCII). They do not check the voice of a new page's words, so each of the three new test modules holds its templates to it: no em dash, no exclamation mark, none of the words `pages/tests_chapters.py` bans.
7. **`pages.tests_site_rules.test_every_component_has_a_stylesheet_and_a_catalog_entry` fails while a component lacks its sheet, its link in `shell.html` or its catalog entry**, so Step 3 makes the four together.
8. **Nothing in Overview may call Stripe.** `status` reads our own tables (`StatusView` makes no Stripe call), and a test shuts the network.

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the meter's tests**

Create `backend/pages/tests_meter.py`. Every class sets `longMessage = False` (Step 8 lists the module where `pages.tests_site_rules` holds it to that), and every message names the file and the fix.

```python
"""The meter (spec 4.8, 6.2): one figure of the dashboard against its limit, as a mono label, the numbers in words and a hairline bar.

The numbers are always in the text, so the bar adds nothing a reader would miss. The bar itself is `role="meter"` (what a native <meter> means,
and not a progress bar, which says a task is under way), named by the label and described by the figures, over an SVG drawn from attributes:
a page may not carry an inline style. Every class sets longMessage = False and says which file to fix.
"""
import re
from pathlib import Path

from django.conf import settings
from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.template.loader import render_to_string
from django.test import SimpleTestCase, TestCase

from pages import catalog
from pages.tests_chapters import BANNED
from pages.tests_reading import declarations, rules
from pages.tests_shell import render_shell

STATIC = Path(settings.BASE_DIR) / "static"
FILE = "backend/templates/components/meter.html"
CSS = "backend/static/css/components/meter.css"
GB = 1024**3


def meter(**inputs):
    """components/meter.html as a page includes it: with these inputs and nothing else."""
    return render_to_string("components/meter.html", {"id": "t-one", "label": "Successful uploads this month", "used": 37, "cap": 100, **inputs})


def figures(html):
    """The words of the figures line as a reader sees them."""
    found = re.search(r'<p class="meter__figures" id="[^"]*">(.*?)</p>', html, re.S)
    assert found, f"{FILE}: a meter has a <p class=\"meter__figures\" id=...> line"
    return " ".join(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", found.group(1)).split())


def bar(html):
    """The attributes of the bar (the element with role=meter), or None when there is none."""
    found = re.search(r'<div ([^>]*class="meter__bar"[^>]*)>', html)
    return dict(re.findall(r'([\w-]+)="([^"]*)"', found.group(1))) if found else None


class MeterTests(SimpleTestCase):
    longMessage = False

    def test_a_figure_with_a_limit_is_a_label_the_numbers_and_a_bar_that_names_both(self):
        html = meter()
        self.assertIn('<p class="meter__label label" id="t-one_label">Successful uploads this month</p>', html,
                      f'{FILE}: the label is <p class="meter__label label" id="<id>_label"> (mono, uppercase, muted: base.css .label)')
        self.assertEqual(figures(html), "37 of 100", f"{FILE}: the figures say used of cap, in words")
        attrs = bar(html)
        self.assertEqual(attrs, {"class": "meter__bar", "role": "meter", "aria-labelledby": "t-one_label", "aria-describedby": "t-one_figures",
                                 "aria-valuemin": "0", "aria-valuemax": "100", "aria-valuenow": "37"},
                         f'{FILE}: the bar is role="meter", named by the label, described by the figures, with its minimum, maximum and value; found {attrs}')
        self.assertIn('<svg viewBox="0 0 1000 1" preserveAspectRatio="none" aria-hidden="true"><rect class="meter__fill" width="370" height="1"/></svg>', html,
                      f"{FILE}: the fill is a rect whose width is the figure in thousandths of the limit (37 of 100 is 370 of 1000), in a viewBox 1000 wide, hidden from screen readers (the text says the numbers)")
        self.assertLess(html.index("meter__label"), html.index("meter__figures"))
        self.assertLess(html.index("meter__figures"), html.index("meter__bar"), f"{FILE}: label, figures, bar, in that order")

    def test_the_names_the_bar_points_at_exist_on_the_page(self):
        html = meter(id="catalog-x-0")
        for token in (bar(html)["aria-labelledby"], bar(html)["aria-describedby"]):
            self.assertEqual(html.count(f'id="{token}"'), 1, f"{FILE}: aria-labelledby and aria-describedby name ids that the component prints once, built from its id input")

    def test_sizes_are_written_by_the_bytes_filter_and_the_bar_is_drawn_in_bytes(self):
        html = meter(label="Storage", used=GB * 3 // 2, cap=25 * GB, unit="bytes")
        self.assertEqual(figures(html), "1.5 GB of 25.0 GB", f"{FILE}: with unit=bytes, used and cap go through the bytes filter (1024 base, one decimal)")
        self.assertEqual(bar(html)["aria-valuemax"], str(25 * GB), f"{FILE}: the bar's numbers are bytes, not the words")
        self.assertIn('viewBox="0 0 1000 1"', html, f"{FILE}: the viewBox is 1000 wide whatever the limit, so a size in bytes never puts a number of ten digits in a coordinate")
        self.assertIn('<rect class="meter__fill" width="60" height="1"/>', html, f"{FILE}: 1.5 GB of 25 GB is 60 thousandths")
        self.assertEqual(figures(meter(used=0, cap=GB, unit="bytes")), "0 B of 1.0 GB", f"{FILE}: nothing used is 0 B")

    def test_counts_are_grouped_in_the_words_and_plain_in_the_bar(self):
        html = meter(used=1234, cap=10000)
        self.assertEqual(figures(html), "1,234 of 10,000", f"{FILE}: print counts with floatformat:\"0g\", which groups by thousands")
        self.assertEqual((bar(html)["aria-valuenow"], bar(html)["aria-valuemax"]), ("1234", "10000"), f"{FILE}: the bar's attributes are plain numbers")

    def test_over_its_limit_the_figures_say_so_in_words_and_the_bar_stays_full(self):
        html = meter(label="API keys", used=7, cap=5)
        self.assertEqual(figures(html), "7 of 5 Over the limit", f"{FILE}: past the cap the figures end with Over the limit, in words, not in colour")
        self.assertIn('<span class="meter__flag label">Over the limit</span>', html)
        self.assertTrue(html.lstrip().startswith('<div class="meter meter--over">'), f"{FILE}: the wrapper takes meter--over, which the stylesheet draws the bar's line solid for")
        self.assertEqual((bar(html)["aria-valuenow"], bar(html)["aria-valuemax"]), ("5", "5"), f"{FILE}: a meter's value cannot pass its maximum, so the bar is full at the cap")
        self.assertIn('<rect class="meter__fill" width="1000" height="1"/>', html, f"{FILE}: past the cap the fill is the whole bar")
        self.assertIn("7 of 5", html, f"{FILE}: the words keep the true figure, for the description")

    def test_at_its_limit_is_full_and_not_over(self):
        html = meter(used=5, cap=5)
        self.assertEqual(figures(html), "5 of 5")
        self.assertNotIn("meter--over", html, f"{FILE}: only a figure past its cap is over")
        self.assertNotIn("Over the limit", html)

    def test_no_limit_says_unlimited_in_words_and_draws_no_bar(self):
        html = meter(label="API keys", used=3, cap=None, unlimited=True)
        self.assertEqual(figures(html), "3 of unlimited", f"{FILE}: with unlimited and no cap the figures say of unlimited")
        self.assertIsNone(bar(html), f"{FILE}: no limit, nothing to fill: draw no bar")
        self.assertNotIn("<svg", html)
        self.assertNotIn("meter--over", html)

    def test_a_cap_given_with_unlimited_is_still_a_cap(self):
        self.assertEqual(figures(meter(used=3, cap=5, unlimited=True)), "3 of 5", f"{FILE}: unlimited only speaks when there is no cap")

    def test_a_figure_with_no_limit_and_a_unit_is_a_value(self):
        self.assertEqual(figures(meter(label="Links last up to", used=7, cap=None, unit="day")), "7 days", f"{FILE}: a unit word follows the number, plural when it should be")
        self.assertEqual(figures(meter(used=1, cap=None, unit="day")), "1 day")
        self.assertIsNone(bar(meter(used=7, cap=None, unit="day")), f"{FILE}: a value with no limit has no bar")

    def test_a_cap_of_zero_draws_no_bar(self):
        html = meter(used=0, cap=0)
        self.assertEqual(figures(html), "0 of 0")
        self.assertIsNone(bar(html), f"{FILE}: a bar needs a limit above 0; a viewBox 0 wide draws nothing and fails to render")

    def test_a_note_is_a_line_under_the_bar(self):
        html = meter(note="Counted by calendar month, in UTC.")
        self.assertIn('<p class="meter__note">Counted by calendar month, in UTC.</p>', html, f"{FILE}: note is printed under the bar")
        self.assertLess(html.index("meter__bar"), html.index("meter__note"))
        self.assertNotIn("meter__note", meter(), f"{FILE}: no note, no line")

    def test_words_are_escaped(self):
        html = meter(label='<b>Uploads</b> & "more"', note="<i>x</i>")
        for raw in ("<b>", "<i>"):
            self.assertNotIn(raw, html, f"{FILE}: print the label and the note escaped")
        self.assertIn("&lt;b&gt;Uploads&lt;/b&gt; &amp; &quot;more&quot;", html)

    def test_the_template_keeps_the_voice(self):
        text = (Path(settings.BASE_DIR) / "templates" / "components" / "meter.html").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        words = re.sub(r"{%.*?%}|{#.*?#}|{{.*?}}", "", text)  # a template tag may say != ; the words may not shout
        self.assertNotIn("\N{EM DASH}", text, f"{FILE}: no em dashes; use a colon, a comma or two sentences")
        self.assertNotIn("!", words, f"{FILE}: no exclamation marks")
        for word in BANNED:
            self.assertNotIn(word, text.lower(), f"{FILE}: avoid {word.strip()!r} (AGENTS.md, voice)")

    def test_nothing_is_styled_inline(self):
        for inputs in ({}, {"used": 9, "cap": 5}, {"cap": None, "unlimited": True}, {"unit": "bytes", "used": GB, "cap": 2 * GB}):
            with self.subTest(inputs=inputs):
                self.assertNotRegex(meter(**inputs), r"\sstyle\s*=", f"{FILE}: no style attribute; the fill's width is an SVG attribute (tests_site_rules holds every shell template to it)")


class MeterCssTests(SimpleTestCase):
    longMessage = False

    def setUp(self):
        self.css = (STATIC / "css" / "components" / "meter.css").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    def test_the_sheet_is_linked_after_base_css(self):
        html = render_shell()
        link = 'href="/static/css/components/meter.css"'
        self.assertIn(link, html, "backend/templates/shell.html: link css/components/meter.css with the other component sheets")
        self.assertGreater(html.index(link), html.index('href="/static/css/base.css"'),
                           "backend/templates/shell.html: link css/components/meter.css after css/base.css, so the component's rules come last")

    def test_the_bar_is_a_hairline_box_filled_with_ink(self):
        box = declarations(self.css, ".meter .meter__bar")
        self.assertEqual(box.get("border"), "1px solid var(--hair)", f"{CSS}: the bar is a 1px --hair box, as the code block and the main action are")
        self.assertEqual(box.get("background"), "var(--box)")
        fill = next(properties for selectors, properties in rules(self.css) if ".meter .meter__fill" in selectors)  # the first rule: the forced-colours one comes after
        self.assertEqual(fill.get("fill"), "var(--ink)", f"{CSS}: the fill is --ink")
        self.assertEqual(declarations(self.css, ".meter--over .meter__bar").get("border-color"), "var(--ink)", f"{CSS}: over its cap the bar's line goes solid --ink (no colour is added)")

    def test_a_forced_colours_screen_keeps_the_fill(self):
        self.assertRegex(self.css, r"@media \(forced-colors: active\) \{\s*\.meter \.meter__fill \{\s*fill: CanvasText;",
                         f"{CSS}: in forced colours the fill takes the system text colour, or it may match the box and show a full bar")

    def test_nothing_moves_or_stacks(self):
        for selectors, properties in rules(self.css):
            for name in ("z-index", "opacity", "transition", "animation", "position", "filter", "will-change"):
                self.assertNotIn(name, properties, f"{CSS}: `{selectors[0]}` sets {name}; a meter is still, in the page's flow, and must not make <main> a backdrop root (AGENTS.md, Site checks)")

    def test_the_sheet_has_no_colour_but_tokens_and_no_em_dash(self):
        self.assertNotRegex(self.css, r"#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}\b|\b(?:rgba?|hsla?|oklch|lab|lch)\(", f"{CSS}: colours come from tokens.css")
        self.assertNotIn("\N{EM DASH}", self.css, f"{CSS}: no em dash, in comments too")


class MeterCatalogTests(TestCase):
    longMessage = False

    def setUp(self):
        staff = get_user_model().objects.create_user("meter-staff", "meter-staff@example.com", "a-test-only-password", is_staff=True)
        self.client.force_login(staff)
        self.html = self.client.get("/app/components/").content.decode()
        self.entry = next(entry for entry in catalog.entries() if entry.name == "meter")
        self.samples = (self.entry.context, *self.entry.states)

    def test_the_catalog_shows_a_figure_with_a_limit_in_bytes_over_its_limit_with_none_and_a_value(self):
        used_over = [s for s in self.samples if s.get("cap") and s["used"] > s["cap"]]
        self.assertTrue(used_over, "backend/pages/catalog.py: the meter's Entry shows a figure over 100% of its cap")
        self.assertTrue([s for s in self.samples if s.get("unlimited") and s.get("cap") is None], "backend/pages/catalog.py: the meter's Entry shows unlimited")
        self.assertTrue([s for s in self.samples if s.get("unit") == "bytes"], "backend/pages/catalog.py: the meter's Entry shows a size")
        self.assertTrue([s for s in self.samples if s.get("cap") is None and not s.get("unlimited")], "backend/pages/catalog.py: the meter's Entry shows a value with no limit")
        self.assertEqual(len({s["id"] for s in self.samples}), len(self.samples), "backend/pages/catalog.py: each state needs an id of its own")

    def test_every_state_is_drawn_in_every_frame(self):
        for sample in self.samples:
            for frame in range(4):
                with self.subTest(state=sample["id"], frame=frame):
                    self.assertIn(f'id="{sample["id"]}-{frame}_label"', self.html, "backend/pages/catalog.py: the frame draws every state of the meter, numbered by frame")

    def test_the_meters_are_shown_inside_their_list(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.entry.within, "meters", 'backend/pages/catalog.py: pass within="meters" to the meter Entry, so the states stack in the width the Overview gives them')
        self.assertEqual(self.html.count('<div class="meters">'), 4)

    def test_the_bars_and_the_over_flags_are_counted(self):
        with_bar = len([s for s in self.samples if s.get("cap")])
        self.assertEqual(self.html.count('role="meter"'), 4 * with_bar, "backend/pages/catalog.py: a state with a cap draws one bar in each of the four frames")
        over = len([s for s in self.samples if s.get("cap") and s["used"] > s["cap"]])
        self.assertEqual(self.html.count("Over the limit"), 4 * over)
```

- [ ] **Step 3: The meter**

Four pieces together (Fact 7). First the template. A component starts with its two comments; the figures line is one line, so no stray white space sits between the words.

Create `backend/templates/components/meter.html`:

```django
{# Component: meter. One figure of the dashboard against its limit (spec 4.8): a mono label, the numbers in words and, when there is a limit, a hairline bar that fills as the figure nears it, to the thousandth. #}
{# Inputs: id, unique on the page (the label's id is the id and _label, the figures' the id and _figures); label, the words above; used, a whole number; cap, the limit, a whole number or none; unit, bytes (used and cap are printed as B, KB, MB or GB), a word such as day (printed after the number, plural when it should be) or absent for a plain count; unlimited, true to print of unlimited when there is no cap; note, a short line under the bar. Over its cap the figure says so in words and the bar stays full. A figure with no cap that is not unlimited, such as how long links last, has no bar. #}
{% load dashboard %}<div class="meter{% if cap and used > cap %} meter--over{% endif %}">
<p class="meter__label label" id="{{ id }}_label">{{ label }}</p>
<p class="meter__figures" id="{{ id }}_figures">{% if unit == "bytes" %}{{ used|bytes }}{% else %}{{ used|floatformat:"0g" }}{% if unit %} {{ unit }}{{ used|pluralize }}{% endif %}{% endif %}{% if cap is not None %} of {% if unit == "bytes" %}{{ cap|bytes }}{% else %}{{ cap|floatformat:"0g" }}{% endif %}{% elif unlimited %} of unlimited{% endif %}{% if cap and used > cap %} <span class="meter__flag label">Over the limit</span>{% endif %}</p>
{% if cap %}{% widthratio used cap 1000 as share %}<div class="meter__bar" role="meter" aria-labelledby="{{ id }}_label" aria-describedby="{{ id }}_figures" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="{{ cap }}" aria-valuenow="{% if used > cap %}{{ cap }}{% else %}{{ used }}{% endif %}">
<svg viewBox="0 0 1000 1" preserveAspectRatio="none" aria-hidden="true"><rect class="meter__fill" width="{% if used > cap %}1000{% else %}{{ share }}{% endif %}" height="1"/></svg>
</div>
{% endif %}{% if note %}<p class="meter__note">{{ note }}</p>
{% endif %}</div>
```

Its stylesheet. Colours are tokens, the rules weigh two classes so that Task 2's bare element rules for a layout never beat them, and nothing in it moves, stacks or sets an opacity.

Create `backend/static/css/components/meter.css`:

```css
/* A meter (spec 4.8): one figure of the dashboard against its limit. A mono label, the numbers in words, and under them a hairline bar: a 1px
   --hair box on --box, filled with --ink as far as the figure goes. The bar is an SVG whose fill is a width attribute (the viewBox is 1000
   wide and the fill is the figure in thousandths of the limit), because a page may not carry an inline style, and a native <meter> is drawn
   through a pseudo-element of each engine that nothing here can look at; the box is a border, which a forced-colours screen keeps. Over its
   limit the bar stays full, its line goes solid --ink and the figures say Over the limit in words: no colour, weight and a word, as a form's
   error has. Rules weigh two classes so that a layout's bare element rules (a paragraph's margin) never win. Nothing here moves, sets a
   z-index or an opacity. */
.meters {
  width: 100%;
  min-width: 0;
}

.meter {
  min-width: 0;
  margin: 0 0 var(--space-4);
  font-variant-numeric: lining-nums;
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}

.meter:last-child {
  margin-bottom: 0;
}

.meter .meter__label {
  display: block;
  margin: 0 0 var(--space-1);
}

.meter .meter__figures {
  margin: 0 0 var(--space-2);
  color: var(--ink);
}

.meter .meter__flag {
  margin-left: var(--space-2);
  color: var(--ink);
}

.meter .meter__bar {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  height: .5rem;
  border: 1px solid var(--hair);
  background: var(--box);
}

.meter .meter__bar svg {
  display: block;
  width: 100%;
  height: 100%;
  shape-rendering: crispEdges;
}

.meter .meter__fill {
  fill: var(--ink);
}

.meter--over .meter__bar {
  border-color: var(--ink);
}

.meter .meter__note {
  margin: var(--space-2) 0 0;
  font-size: .9em;
  color: var(--muted);
}

/* The system's own text colour for the fill, so it stays seen where the page's colours are replaced. */
@media (forced-colors: active) {
  .meter .meter__fill {
    fill: CanvasText;
  }
}
```

Create `backend/dashboard/tests_overview.py`. Its helpers read the page as a visitor does (`Tree` and `words` are the reset pages' test helpers, imported, not copied). The sentences it holds are the React dashboard's, each in a constant at the top, so a change of words is one edit and shows in the diff.

```python
"""Overview (spec 4.8): the first page of the dashboard, at /app/.

In this order: the notice a visitor returns from Stripe with (?billing=), the prompt to verify an email, anything over a limit, the plan,
the meters (uploads this month, storage, API keys, how long links last) and the account (its email, whether it is verified, and the links
to change the email and the password). The numbers come from the account functions that the JSON endpoints answer with (drop_core.account.usage
and drop_billing.account.status, which makes no Stripe call); the words are the template's. A read that fails leaves out its own part and
nothing else.

Every class sets longMessage = False (pages.tests_site_rules holds this module to it): a failed assertIn on a page would print the page before the
message, so each message names the file to fix and what was found.
"""
import re
import socket
from datetime import timedelta
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

from django.conf import settings
from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.test import Client, SimpleTestCase, TestCase
from django.utils import timezone

from drop_core.account import Answer
from drop_core.models import APIKey, Artifact, EmailVerification, UsageCounter, get_or_create_workspace
from drop_core.plans import PLANS
from drop_core.tests_reset_verify_pages import Tree, in_main, words
from pages.tests_chapters import BANNED

User = get_user_model()
PASSWORD = "pw12345678"
GB = 1024**3
VIEW = "backend/dashboard/overview_page.py"
PAGE = "backend/templates/dashboard/overview.html"
OVER = "backend/templates/dashboard/over_limits.html"

# The sentences the React dashboard said, kept word for word where they still apply (the skeleton's copy rule).
SUCCESS = "Subscription updated. It can take a moment for the new plan to appear below. Refresh if it doesn't."
CANCELLED = "Checkout was cancelled. No charges were made."
ERROR = "We couldn't start checkout{plan}. Nothing was charged. Try again from Billing."
ALREADY = "You already have a subscription, so no new checkout was started. Switch plans or manage billing."
VERIFY = "Verify your email to create API keys."
KEYS_OVER = "{n} active API keys; the plan allows {cap}. Existing keys keep working, but new keys can't be created until you revoke some or upgrade."
STORAGE_OVER = "{used} stored; the plan allows {cap} GB. Existing links keep working, but new uploads are refused until you're under the cap."
TTL_OVER = "Some links expire later than the plan's {days}-day maximum. They keep their original expiry; new uploads get at most {days} days."
UPLOADS_OVER = "{used} uploads this month; the plan allows {cap}. Existing links keep working, but new uploads are refused until the next month begins (UTC)."
BILLING_DOWN = "Plan limits could not be checked just now. Reload the page to check again."
USAGE_DOWN = "Usage could not be loaded just now. Reload the page to try again."


def make_user(name, email="", verified=None, plan="free"):
    """A user with a workspace on `plan`. `verified` is None for no verification record, else whether the record is verified."""
    user = User.objects.create_user(username=name, email=email, password=PASSWORD)
    workspace = get_or_create_workspace(user)
    if plan != "free":
        workspace.plan = plan
        workspace.save(update_fields=["plan"])
    if verified is not None:
        EmailVerification.objects.create(user=user, email=email, is_verified=verified, verified_at=timezone.now() if verified else None)
    return user, workspace


def this_month():
    return timezone.now().strftime("%Y-%m")  # the upload counter's month is the UTC month


def artifact(workspace, name, size, days):
    return Artifact.objects.create(workspace=workspace, filename=name, size_bytes=size, expires_at=timezone.now() + timedelta(days=days))


class Overview:
    """A response of /app/ read as a visitor reads it."""

    def __init__(self, response):
        self.response = response
        self.html = response.content.decode()
        self.tree = Tree(self.html)
        self.main = self.tree.all("main")[0]
        self.text = words(self.main)

    def classed(self, name, tag=None):
        return [e for e in self.tree.elements if in_main(e) and name in e["attrs"].get("class", "").split() and tag in (None, e["tag"])]

    def notices(self):
        """(role, words) of each .notice in <main>, in order."""
        return [(e["attrs"].get("role"), words(e)) for e in self.classed("notice")]

    def sections(self):
        """{heading: words of its section}, in order: every <section> of <main> is named by its h2."""
        ids = self.tree.ids()
        return {words(ids[e["attrs"]["aria-labelledby"]]): words(e) for e in self.tree.all("section") if in_main(e)}

    def meters(self):
        """[(label, figures)] in order."""
        return [(words(label), words(figures)) for label, figures in zip(self.classed("meter__label"), self.classed("meter__figures"))]

    def bars(self):
        return [e["attrs"] for e in self.tree.elements if e["attrs"].get("role") == "meter"]

    def links(self):
        return [(words(e), e["attrs"].get("href")) for e in self.tree.all("a") if in_main(e)]


class OverviewTestCase(TestCase):
    longMessage = False

    def open(self, user, query=""):
        client = Client()
        client.force_login(user)
        response = client.get("/app/" + query)
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200, f"{PAGE}: /app/ answers 200 for a signed-in visitor, found {response.status_code}")
        return Overview(response)


class OverviewPageTests(OverviewTestCase):
    def test_one_h1_overview_then_the_plan_the_usage_and_the_account(self):
        user, _ = make_user("ov-shape", "shape@example.com", verified=True)
        page = self.open(user)
        h1s = page.tree.all("h1")
        self.assertEqual([words(h) for h in h1s], ["Overview"], f"{PAGE}: one <h1>, Overview, inside <main>")
        self.assertTrue(in_main(h1s[0]))
        self.assertEqual(list(page.sections()), ["Plan", "Usage", "Account"], f"{PAGE}: three sections, each a <section aria-labelledby> named by its <h2>, in this order")
        for element in page.tree.elements:
            if element["tag"] in ("header", "footer"):
                self.assertFalse(in_main(element), f"{PAGE}: no <{element['tag']}> inside <main> (spec 9)")

    def test_the_page_is_kept_out_of_search(self):
        user, _ = make_user("ov-robots", "robots@example.com", verified=True)
        page = self.open(user)
        self.assertIn('<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">', page.html, "backend/templates/layouts/app.html: every dashboard page carries the noindex tag, which the layout puts in the head's meta block (Task 2)")
        self.assertEqual(page.response["X-Robots-Tag"], "noindex, nofollow", "backend/dashboard/views.py: overview is wrapped in dashboard_view")

    def test_a_fresh_free_account_shows_its_four_figures(self):
        user, _ = make_user("ov-fresh", "fresh@example.com", verified=True)
        page = self.open(user)
        self.assertEqual(page.meters(), [("Successful uploads this month", "0 of 100"), ("Storage", "0 B of 1.0 GB"), ("API keys", "0 of 1"), ("Links last up to", "7 days")],
                         f"{PAGE}: the four figures, from usage (drop_core.account.usage)")
        self.assertEqual(len(page.bars()), 3, f"{PAGE}: uploads, storage and keys have a bar; how long links last is a value with no limit")
        for bar in page.bars():
            self.assertIn(bar["aria-labelledby"], page.tree.ids(), f"{PAGE}: each bar is named by its label")
        self.assertIn("Counted by calendar month, in UTC.", page.sections()["Usage"], f"{PAGE}: the uploads figure says that its month is the UTC month")
        self.assertIn("You are on the Free plan.", page.sections()["Plan"])
        self.assertIn(("Billing", "/app/billing/"), page.links(), f"{PAGE}: the plan section links to Billing")

    def test_a_team_account_with_some_use(self):
        user, workspace = make_user("ov-team", "team@example.com", verified=True, plan="team")
        UsageCounter.objects.create(workspace=workspace, year_month=this_month(), uploads=1234)
        UsageCounter.objects.create(workspace=workspace, year_month="1999-01", uploads=99)  # another month is not this month's figure
        APIKey.create_key(workspace, "ci")
        APIKey.create_key(workspace, "laptop")
        artifact(workspace, "report.pdf", GB * 3 // 2, 30)
        page = self.open(user)
        self.assertEqual(page.meters(), [("Successful uploads this month", "1,234 of 2,000"), ("Storage", "1.5 GB of 25.0 GB"), ("API keys", "2 of 5"), ("Links last up to", "90 days")])
        self.assertIn("You are on the Team plan.", page.sections()["Plan"])
        self.assertNotIn("Your workspace is over", page.text, f"{VIEW}: nothing is over, so there are no limit lines")
        self.assertEqual(page.notices(), [], f"{PAGE}: a clean account has no notice")

    def test_a_scale_account_has_unlimited_keys_and_no_bar_for_them(self):
        user, workspace = make_user("ov-scale", "scale@example.com", verified=True, plan="scale")
        APIKey.create_key(workspace, "one")
        APIKey.create_key(workspace, "two")
        page = self.open(user)
        self.assertEqual(page.meters()[2:], [("API keys", "2 of unlimited"), ("Links last up to", "365 days")])
        self.assertEqual(page.meters()[0], ("Successful uploads this month", "0 of 10,000"))
        self.assertEqual(len(page.bars()), 2, f"{PAGE}: with no key limit there is no bar for keys: pass unlimited=True to the meter")

    def test_the_figures_are_the_visitors_own(self):
        _, other = make_user("ov-other", "other@example.com", verified=True)
        for i in range(3):
            APIKey.create_key(other, f"key {i}")
        user, _ = make_user("ov-mine", "mine@example.com", verified=True)
        page = self.open(user)
        self.assertEqual(page.meters()[2], ("API keys", "0 of 1"), f"{VIEW}: the figures are the signed-in user's workspace, nobody else's")

    def test_everything_comes_in_the_order_the_spec_gives(self):
        user, workspace = make_user("ov-order", "order@example.com", verified=False)
        for i in range(2):
            APIKey.create_key(workspace, f"key {i}")
        page = self.open(user, "?billing=error&plan=scale")
        marks = ["We couldn't start checkout for the Scale plan.", VERIFY, "Your workspace is over the free plan's limits.", "You are on the Free plan.",
                 "Successful uploads this month", "not verified."]
        found = [page.text.find(mark) for mark in marks]
        self.assertTrue(all(i >= 0 for i in found), f"{PAGE}: all of {marks} are on this page; found at {found}")
        self.assertEqual(found, sorted(found), f"{PAGE}: the return notice, the verify prompt, what is over a limit, the plan, the meters and the account, in that order; found at {found}")
        self.assertLess(page.text.index("Overview"), found[0], f"{PAGE}: the h1 comes first")


class OverLimitTests(OverviewTestCase):
    def over_text(self, page):
        found = [words(e) for e in page.classed("notice") if "Your workspace is over" in words(e)]
        self.assertEqual(len(found), 1, f"{PAGE}: one block says the workspace is over, found {len(found)}: {found}")
        return found[0]

    def test_a_workspace_over_nothing_says_nothing(self):
        user, workspace = make_user("ov-within", "within@example.com", verified=True)
        APIKey.create_key(workspace, "only")
        page = self.open(user)
        self.assertNotIn("Your workspace is over", page.text, f"{OVER}: the lines are drawn only when something is over")

    def test_after_a_downgrade_every_limit_is_named_first_in_the_old_words(self):
        user, workspace = make_user("ov-down", "down@example.com", verified=True)
        for i in range(3):
            APIKey.create_key(workspace, f"key {i}")
        artifact(workspace, "big.bin", 2 * GB, 300)
        UsageCounter.objects.create(workspace=workspace, year_month=this_month(), uploads=150)
        page = self.open(user)
        block = page.classed("notice")[0]
        self.assertEqual(block["attrs"].get("role"), "status", f'{OVER}: the lines are a .notice with role="status", the first notice of the page')
        said = words(block)
        self.assertTrue(said.startswith("Your workspace is over the free plan's limits."), f"{OVER}: it opens with the old sentence, naming the plan; found {said!r}")
        for sentence in (KEYS_OVER.format(n=3, cap=1), STORAGE_OVER.format(used="2.0 GB", cap=1), TTL_OVER.format(days=7), UPLOADS_OVER.format(used=150, cap=100)):
            self.assertIn(sentence, said, f"{OVER}: keep the sentence {sentence!r}")
        self.assertLess(page.text.index("Your workspace is over"), page.text.index("You are on the Free plan."), f"{PAGE}: anything over a limit comes before the plan (spec 4.8)")
        self.assertNotIn("section", [p["tag"] for p in block["parents"]], f"{PAGE}: the lines are not inside a section: they come first")
        self.assertEqual([label for label, figures in page.meters() if "Over the limit" in figures], ["Successful uploads this month", "Storage", "API keys"],
                         f"{PAGE}: the meters that are over say so in words")
        self.assertEqual((workspace.api_keys.filter(is_active=True).count(), workspace.artifacts.count()), (3, 1), "nothing is revoked or deleted for being over")

    def test_each_limit_has_a_line_of_its_own(self):
        cases = {}
        user, workspace = make_user("ov-keys", "keys@example.com", verified=True)
        APIKey.create_key(workspace, "a")
        APIKey.create_key(workspace, "b")
        cases["keys"] = (user, [KEYS_OVER.format(n=2, cap=1)])
        user, workspace = make_user("ov-storage", "storage@example.com", verified=True)
        artifact(workspace, "big.bin", 2 * GB, 3)
        cases["storage"] = (user, [STORAGE_OVER.format(used="2.0 GB", cap=1)])
        user, workspace = make_user("ov-ttl", "ttl@example.com", verified=True)
        artifact(workspace, "slow.bin", 10, 30)
        cases["ttl"] = (user, [TTL_OVER.format(days=7)])
        user, workspace = make_user("ov-uploads", "uploads@example.com", verified=True)
        UsageCounter.objects.create(workspace=workspace, year_month=this_month(), uploads=101)
        cases["uploads"] = (user, [UPLOADS_OVER.format(used=101, cap=100)])
        for name, (user, sentences) in cases.items():
            with self.subTest(over=name):
                said = self.over_text(self.open(user))
                for sentence in sentences:
                    self.assertIn(sentence, said, f"{OVER}: the {name} line is {sentence!r}")
                self.assertEqual(said.count("; the plan allows") + said.count("Some links expire"), 1, f"{OVER}: only the {name} line, found {said!r}")

    def test_the_heading_names_the_plan_the_workspace_is_on(self):
        user, workspace = make_user("ov-teamover", "teamover@example.com", verified=True, plan="team")
        for i in range(6):
            APIKey.create_key(workspace, f"key {i}")
        said = self.over_text(self.open(user))
        self.assertTrue(said.startswith("Your workspace is over the team plan's limits."), f"{OVER}: the plan is named as the old dashboard named it; found {said!r}")
        self.assertIn(KEYS_OVER.format(n=6, cap=5), said)


class BillingReturnTests(OverviewTestCase):
    """?billing= is the address Stripe and sign up send people back with (drop_billing/views.py): four values, four notices."""

    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        self.user, _ = make_user("ov-return", "return@example.com", verified=True)

    def test_each_of_the_four_says_what_the_old_dashboard_said(self):
        cases = {
            "success": ("status", SUCCESS),
            "cancelled": ("status", CANCELLED),
            "error": ("alert", ERROR.format(plan="")),
            "already_subscribed": ("status", ALREADY),
        }
        for value, (role, sentence) in cases.items():
            with self.subTest(billing=value):
                page = self.open(self.user, f"?billing={value}")
                self.assertEqual(page.notices(), [(role, sentence)], f'{PAGE}: ?billing={value} shows one .notice, role="{role}": {sentence!r}')

    def test_the_sentences_that_pointed_below_point_at_billing(self):
        page = self.open(self.user, "?billing=error")
        self.assertIn(("Billing", "/app/billing/"), page.links(), f"{PAGE}: Billing is another page now, so the error notice links to it instead of saying below")
        page = self.open(self.user, "?billing=already_subscribed")
        self.assertIn(("Switch plans or manage billing", "/app/billing/"), page.links())

    def test_any_other_value_shows_nothing(self):
        for value in ("", "nope", "SUCCESS", "success%20", "error%00", "<script>", "success&billing=x"):
            with self.subTest(billing=value):
                page = self.open(self.user, f"?billing={value}")
                self.assertEqual(page.notices(), [], f"{VIEW}: only success, cancelled, error and already_subscribed are notices")

    def test_the_error_names_the_plan_only_when_it_is_a_paid_plan_of_plans_py(self):
        for plan, name in (("team", " for the Team plan"), ("scale", " for the Scale plan")):
            with self.subTest(plan=plan):
                self.assertEqual(self.open(self.user, f"?billing=error&plan={plan}").notices(), [("alert", ERROR.format(plan=name))])
        for plan in ("free", "", "TEAM", "team%20", "enterprise", "%3Cscript%3Ealert(1)%3C/script%3E", "..%2Fx", "team%00", "constructor"):
            with self.subTest(plan=plan):
                page = self.open(self.user, f"?billing=error&plan={plan}")
                self.assertEqual(page.notices(), [("alert", ERROR.format(plan=""))], f"{VIEW}: a plan that is not a paid plan of drop_core/plans.py is not named")
                for raw in ("enterprise", "alert(1)", "constructor", "../x"):
                    self.assertNotIn(raw, page.html, f"{VIEW}: the value of ?plan= is never printed; the name comes from plans.py")

    def test_the_paid_plans_are_the_ones_plans_py_has(self):
        pro = {**PLANS["team"], "price_usd": 9}
        with mock.patch.dict(PLANS, {"pro": pro}):
            page = self.open(self.user, "?billing=error&plan=pro")
        self.assertEqual(page.notices(), [("alert", ERROR.format(plan=" for the Pro plan"))],
                         f"{VIEW}: check ?plan= against plans.PLANS (a plan with a price), not against a list written in the view")

    def test_the_other_notices_ignore_the_plan(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.open(self.user, "?billing=success&plan=team").notices(), [("status", SUCCESS)])

    def test_a_notice_is_not_shown_on_a_page_without_the_query(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.open(self.user).notices(), [])


class VerifyPromptTests(OverviewTestCase):
    def prompts(self, page):
        return [(role, said) for role, said in page.notices() if said.startswith(VERIFY)]

    def test_no_address_at_all_asks_for_one(self):
        user, _ = make_user("ov-noaddr")
        page = self.open(user)
        self.assertEqual(self.prompts(page), [(None, f"{VERIFY} Add an email address to your account. Verify email")], f"{PAGE}: the old sentence for an account with no address")
        self.assertIn(("Verify email", "/accounts/verify-email/"), page.links())
```
