```python
class FailureTests(OverviewTestCase):
    """The two reads are separate. One that fails leaves out its own part and puts a sentence there; nothing else goes, and no detail of the failure is printed."""

    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        self.user, self.workspace = make_user("ov-fail", "fail@example.com", verified=True)
        for i in range(3):
            APIKey.create_key(self.workspace, f"key {i}")

    def test_a_billing_status_that_raises_does_not_hide_the_usage(self):
        with mock.patch("drop_billing.account.status", side_effect=RuntimeError("boom: secret detail")), self.assertLogs("dashboard.overview_page", "ERROR") as logs:
            page = self.open(self.user)
        self.assertEqual(page.meters()[2], ("API keys", "3 of 1 Over the limit"), f"{VIEW}: the meters come from usage alone")
        self.assertEqual(len(page.bars()), 3)
        self.assertIn((("status"), BILLING_DOWN), page.notices(), f'{PAGE}: say that the limits could not be checked, as a role="status" notice, where the lines would be')
        self.assertNotIn("Your workspace is over", page.text, f"{PAGE}: with no status there are no limit lines")
        self.assertIn("You are on the Free plan.", page.sections()["Plan"], f"{VIEW}: the plan comes from usage when the status is down")
        for detail in ("boom", "secret detail", "RuntimeError", "Traceback"):
            self.assertNotIn(detail, page.html, f"{VIEW}: never print a failure's detail")
        self.assertTrue(any("boom" in line for line in logs.output), f"{VIEW}: log the failure (logger.exception) so it is found")

    def test_a_billing_status_that_answers_an_error_is_the_same(self):
        with mock.patch("drop_billing.account.status", return_value=Answer(502, {"error": "Stripe: down", "code": "stripe_error"})), self.assertLogs("dashboard.overview_page", "WARNING"):
            page = self.open(self.user)
        self.assertIn(("status", BILLING_DOWN), page.notices())
        self.assertNotIn("Stripe: down", page.html, f"{VIEW}: an error body is not shown")
        self.assertEqual(len(page.meters()), 4)

    def test_no_state_of_the_page_shows_the_operators_words(self):
        # Ruling R1: the dashboard speaks to customers. Stripe's name, its message, a raw error code or "instance" never reach the page, in any state of it.
        banned = ("stripe", "instance", "configured", "traceback", "boom", "card_declined", "acct_", "stripe_error", "billing_not_configured")
        failing = {
            "a Stripe error": mock.patch("drop_billing.account.status", return_value=Answer(502, {"error": "Stripe: card_declined for acct_123", "code": "stripe_error"})),
            "billing not configured": mock.patch("drop_billing.account.status", return_value=Answer(503, {"error": "Billing is not configured on this Veilfile instance.", "code": "billing_not_configured"})),
            "a read that raises": mock.patch("drop_billing.account.status", side_effect=RuntimeError("Stripe: boom on this Veilfile instance")),
        }
        for query in ("", "?billing=success", "?billing=cancelled", "?billing=error", "?billing=error&plan=team", "?billing=already_subscribed"):
            page = self.open(self.user, query)
            for word in banned:
                self.assertNotIn(word, page.text.lower(), f"{PAGE}: {word!r} is operator wording and never shows on Overview (query {query!r})")
            for label, patch in failing.items():
                with patch, self.assertLogs("dashboard.overview_page", "WARNING"):
                    page = self.open(self.user, query)
                self.assertIn(BILLING_DOWN, page.text, f"{PAGE}: {label} ends in the customer sentence {BILLING_DOWN!r} (query {query!r})")
                for word in banned:
                    self.assertNotIn(word, page.text.lower(), f"{PAGE}: {word!r} is operator wording and never shows on Overview, after {label} (query {query!r})")

    def test_the_uploads_line_needs_only_usage(self):
        UsageCounter.objects.create(workspace=self.workspace, year_month=this_month(), uploads=150)
        with mock.patch("drop_billing.account.status", side_effect=RuntimeError("boom")), self.assertLogs("dashboard.overview_page", "ERROR"):
            page = self.open(self.user)
        said = [words(e) for e in page.classed("notice") if "Your workspace is over" in words(e)]
        self.assertEqual(len(said), 1, f"{OVER}: with no status the uploads line still shows, from usage")
        self.assertTrue(said[0].startswith("Your workspace is over the free plan's limits."), f"{OVER}: the plan is named from usage when the status is down; found {said[0]!r}")
        self.assertIn(UPLOADS_OVER.format(used=150, cap=100), said[0])
        self.assertNotIn("active API keys; the plan allows", said[0], f"{OVER}: the keys line needs the status, which is down")
        self.assertIn(("status", BILLING_DOWN), page.notices(), f"{PAGE}: and the page still says that the other limits could not be checked")

    def test_a_usage_that_raises_does_not_hide_the_limits_or_the_account(self):
        with mock.patch("drop_core.account.usage", side_effect=RuntimeError("boom")), self.assertLogs("dashboard.overview_page", "ERROR"):
            page = self.open(self.user)
        self.assertEqual(page.meters(), [], f"{PAGE}: with no usage there are no meters")
        self.assertIn(USAGE_DOWN, page.sections()["Usage"], f"{PAGE}: say so where the meters would be")
        self.assertIn(KEYS_OVER.format(n=3, cap=1), page.text, f"{VIEW}: the limit lines come from the billing status alone")
        self.assertIn("fail@example.com is verified.", page.sections()["Account"])
        self.assertIn("You are on the Free plan.", page.sections()["Plan"], f"{VIEW}: the plan comes from the status when usage is down")

    def test_both_reads_failing_still_draws_the_page(self):
        with mock.patch("drop_core.account.usage", side_effect=RuntimeError("one")), mock.patch("drop_billing.account.status", side_effect=RuntimeError("two")), \
                self.assertLogs("dashboard.overview_page", "ERROR"):
            page = self.open(self.user)
        self.assertEqual([words(h) for h in page.tree.all("h1")], ["Overview"])
        self.assertIn(USAGE_DOWN, page.text)
        self.assertIn(BILLING_DOWN, page.text)
        self.assertNotIn("You are on", page.text, f"{PAGE}: with neither read the plan is not known, so the Plan section is left out")
        self.assertIn("fail@example.com is verified.", page.text)

    def test_the_overview_opens_no_network_connection(self):
        # The billing status is read from our own tables. A call to Stripe here would make the first page of the dashboard wait on a third party and fail with it.
        refuse = AssertionError(f"{VIEW}: the Overview opened a network connection; it may read only our own tables")
        with mock.patch.object(socket.socket, "connect", side_effect=refuse), mock.patch.object(socket.socket, "connect_ex", side_effect=refuse):
            page = self.open(self.user, "?billing=success")
        self.assertEqual(len(page.meters()), 4)
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Overview**

The page's data. `read` is the one place a failed read is caught; `billing_notice` is the one place the `?plan=` is checked; nothing in this module formats a word of the page.

Create `backend/dashboard/overview_page.py`:

```python
"""The Overview page (spec 4.8): what the account has used and what it is over, from the account functions that the JSON endpoints answer with.

Two reads feed it: drop_core.account.usage and drop_billing.account.status (our own tables; it makes no Stripe call). Either may fail, and a read that fails
leaves out its own part of the page, puts a sentence there and nothing else goes: the meters never wait on the billing status, nor the limit lines on usage, nor the
account on either. The failure is logged; its detail is never shown. Which limits the workspace is over is the include's to say (dashboard/over_limits.html), from the two bodies.
"""
import logging

from drop_billing import account as billing_account
from drop_core import account as core_account
from drop_core.email_verification import is_email_verified
from drop_core.models import EmailVerification
from drop_core.plans import PLANS

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# The ?billing= values that Stripe, sign up and checkout send a visitor back with (drop_billing/views.py), and how a screen reader is told of each.
BILLING_NOTICES = {"success": "status", "cancelled": "status", "error": "alert", "already_subscribed": "status"}


def read(function, user, what):
    """The body of an account function's answer, or None when it fails: it raised, or it answered something other than 200. The failure is logged."""
    try:
        answer = function(user)
    except Exception:
        logger.exception("dashboard: the %s could not be read for user %s", what, user.pk)
        return None
    if answer.status != 200:
        logger.warning("dashboard: the %s answered %s for user %s", what, answer.status, user.pk)
        return None
    return answer.body


def billing_notice(query):
    """The notice for ?billing= (and ?plan= for an error), or None for a value that is not one of the four.

    The plan is named only when ?plan= is a plan of drop_core/plans.py with a price, and the name is the plan's id written as the plan cards write it, never the
    text of the query: whatever else is in ?plan= is not printed.
    """
    kind = query.get("billing")
    if kind not in BILLING_NOTICES:
        return None
    plan = query.get("plan") if kind == "error" else ""
    return {"kind": kind, "role": BILLING_NOTICES[kind], "plan": plan.title() if plan in PLANS and PLANS[plan]["price_usd"] > 0 else ""}


def overview_context(request):
    """What templates/dashboard/overview.html is drawn from."""
    user = request.user
    usage = read(core_account.usage, user, "usage")
    status = read(billing_account.status, user, "billing status")
    verified = is_email_verified(user)
    record = EmailVerification.objects.filter(user=user).first()
    return {
        "billing_notice": billing_notice(request.GET),
        # The link went to the address on the verification record, which is not user.email until it is verified (drop_core.views.email_verification).
        "verify_prompt": None if verified else {"sent_to": record.email if record is not None else ""},
        "usage": usage,
        "status": status,
        "plan": (usage or status or {}).get("plan", ""),
        "email": user.email or "",
        "email_verified": verified,
    }
```

The over-limit lines, an include that Billing shares (Task 6 includes this file and does not create it). The sentences are React's; the figures are variables. `status` and `usage` are each a body or `None`, and the comparisons that touch a `None` are false (Fact 4).

Create `backend/templates/dashboard/over_limits.html`:

```django
{# Include: the lines that say a workspace is over what its plan allows, on Overview and Billing (spec 4.8): the React dashboard's OverLimits in its words, and the month's uploads. Nothing is drawn when nothing is over. #}
{# Inputs: status, the body billing.status answers (plan, caps, active_keys, storage_used_bytes, over_plan_limits) or none; usage, the body usage answers or none, for the month's uploads, which the status has no flag for (a page without it leaves that line out). #}
{% load dashboard %}{% if status.over_plan_limits or usage.uploads_used > usage.uploads_cap %}<div class="notice" role="status">
<p><strong>Your workspace is over the {% if status.plan %}{{ status.plan }}{% else %}{{ usage.plan }}{% endif %} plan's limits.</strong></p>
<ul>
{% if "keys" in status.over_plan_limits %}<li>{{ status.active_keys }} active API keys; the plan allows {{ status.caps.keys }}. Existing keys keep working, but new keys can't be created until you revoke some or upgrade.</li>
{% endif %}{% if "storage" in status.over_plan_limits %}<li>{{ status.storage_used_bytes|bytes }} stored; the plan allows {{ status.caps.storage_gb }} GB. Existing links keep working, but new uploads are refused until you're under the cap.</li>
{% endif %}{% if "ttl" in status.over_plan_limits %}<li>Some links expire later than the plan's {{ status.caps.ttl_days }}-day maximum. They keep their original expiry; new uploads get at most {{ status.caps.ttl_days }} days.</li>
{% endif %}{% if usage.uploads_used > usage.uploads_cap %}<li>{{ usage.uploads_used }} uploads this month; the plan allows {{ usage.uploads_cap }}. Existing links keep working, but new uploads are refused until the next month begins (UTC).</li>
{% endif %}</ul>
</div>
{% endif %}
```

```django
{% extends "layouts/app.html" %}
{# Overview: the return from Stripe, the prompt to verify an email, anything over a limit, the plan, the meters and the account, in that order (spec 4.8). The figures come from dashboard/overview_page.py; the words are here. #}
{% block app_main %}
<h1>Overview</h1>
{% if billing_notice.kind == "success" %}<p class="notice" role="status"><strong>Subscription updated.</strong> It can take a moment for the new plan to appear below. Refresh if it doesn't.</p>
{% elif billing_notice.kind == "cancelled" %}<p class="notice" role="status">Checkout was cancelled. No charges were made.</p>
{% elif billing_notice.kind == "error" %}<p class="notice" role="alert"><strong>We couldn't start checkout{% if billing_notice.plan %} for the {{ billing_notice.plan }} plan{% endif %}.</strong> Nothing was charged. Try again from <a href="{% url 'app-billing' %}">Billing</a>.</p>
{% elif billing_notice.kind == "already_subscribed" %}<p class="notice" role="status">You already have a subscription, so no new checkout was started. <a href="{% url 'app-billing' %}">Switch plans or manage billing</a>.</p>
{% endif %}
{% if verify_prompt %}<p class="notice"><strong>Verify your email to create API keys.</strong> {% if verify_prompt.sent_to %}We sent a link to {{ verify_prompt.sent_to }}.{% else %}Add an email address to your account.{% endif %} <a href="{% url 'email-verification' %}">Verify email</a></p>
{% endif %}
{% include "dashboard/over_limits.html" with status=status usage=usage only %}
{% if not status %}<p class="notice" role="status">Plan limits could not be checked just now. Reload the page to check again.</p>
{% endif %}
{% if plan %}<section aria-labelledby="overview-plan">
<h2 id="overview-plan">Plan</h2>
<p>You are on the <strong>{{ plan|title }}</strong> plan. <a href="{% url 'app-billing' %}">Billing</a></p>
</section>
{% endif %}
<section aria-labelledby="overview-usage">
<h2 id="overview-usage">Usage</h2>
{% if usage %}<div class="meters">
{% include "components/meter.html" with id="overview-uploads" label="Successful uploads this month" used=usage.uploads_used cap=usage.uploads_cap note="Counted by calendar month, in UTC." only %}
{% include "components/meter.html" with id="overview-storage" label="Storage" used=usage.storage_used_bytes cap=usage.storage_cap_bytes unit="bytes" only %}
{% include "components/meter.html" with id="overview-keys" label="API keys" used=usage.keys_used cap=usage.keys_cap unlimited=True only %}
{% include "components/meter.html" with id="overview-ttl" label="Links last up to" used=usage.ttl_days unit="day" only %}
</div>
{% else %}<p>Usage could not be loaded just now. Reload the page to try again.</p>
{% endif %}</section>
<section aria-labelledby="overview-account">
<h2 id="overview-account">Account</h2>
{% if email %}<p><strong>{{ email }}</strong> is {% if email_verified %}verified{% else %}not verified{% endif %}.</p>
{% else %}<p>No email address is set.</p>
{% endif %}<p class="form-links"><a class="label interactive" href="{% url 'email-verification' %}">{% if email %}Change email{% else %}Add email{% endif %}</a> <a class="label interactive" href="{% url 'password_change' %}">Change password</a></p>
</section>
{% endblock %}
```

It draws the form, three ways of being sent back, and the page it ends on, each by the real view, and holds them to the rules of the PR 5 form pages (`drop_core.tests_reset_verify_pages`, whose `Tree` it imports). `BehaviourTests` hold what the view does and the sentences claim: the session that changed the password stays and the others end.

```python
"""The password change pages on the form layout (spec 4.7): /accounts/password_change/ and the page it ends on.

Both were the Django admin's pages, in the admin's skin, and nothing linked to them. Overview now links to the first, so they are pages of the site: the shell, one h1,
labelled fields with their errors tied to them, one main action and a quiet way back. The view does not change (drop_core.views.RevokingPasswordChangeView: wrong old passwords
share the login failure budget, and a change disconnects the OAuth apps and keeps the API keys), and its tests (drop_core.tests_fix_auth) pass as they are.

Every class sets longMessage = False (pages.tests_site_rules holds this module to it): a failed assertIn on a page would print the page before the message, so each message
names the file and the fix.
"""
import re
from pathlib import Path

from django.conf import settings
from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.contrib.auth.forms import PasswordChangeForm
from django.contrib.auth.models import AnonymousUser
from django.core.cache import cache
from django.template.loader import render_to_string
from django.test import Client, RequestFactory, TestCase

from drop_core.tests_reset_verify_pages import Tree, in_main, inside, visible_inputs, words
from pages.tests_chapters import BANNED

User = get_user_model()
PASSWORD = "pw12345678"
NEW_PASSWORD = "a-new-pw-98765432"
WRONG_PASSWORD = "wrong-pw-24681357"
FILES = "backend/templates/registration/"
FORM, DONE = "password_change_form.html", "password_change_done.html"
ADDRESS, DONE_ADDRESS = "/accounts/password_change/", "/accounts/password_change/done/"

# state -> (template, the page's name). The title is "<name> | Veilfile" and the name is the h1.
PAGES = {
    "form": (FORM, "Change password"),
    "wrong old password": (FORM, "Change password"),
    "mismatch": (FORM, "Change password"),
    "too short": (FORM, "Change password"),
    "done": (DONE, "Password changed"),
}
FORM_STATES = ("form", "wrong old password", "mismatch", "too short")
INPUTS = [("old_password", "password"), ("new_password1", "password"), ("new_password2", "password")]
LABELS = {"id_old_password": "Current password", "id_new_password1": "New password", "id_new_password2": "Confirm new password"}
TOKENS = {"id_old_password": "current-password", "id_new_password1": "new-password", "id_new_password2": "new-password"}
ERRORS = {  # state -> {input id: a part of the sentence tied to it}; Django's own words, so only the part that matters is held
    "wrong old password": {"id_old_password": "Your old password was entered incorrectly."},
    "mismatch": {"id_new_password2": "The two password fields didn\N{RIGHT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK}t match."},
    "too short": {"id_new_password2": "This password is too short."},
}
INTRO = "Changing your password signs out your other sessions and disconnects your connected apps. API keys keep working."
DONE_WORDS = "Your password is changed. Other sessions were signed out and connected apps were disconnected."


def sign_in(user):
    client = Client()
    client.force_login(user)
    return client


class PageTestCase(TestCase):
    longMessage = False

    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        cache.clear()  # the login failure budget lives in the cache
        self.addCleanup(cache.clear)


class EveryStateTests(PageTestCase):
    """The form, three ways of being sent back, and the page it ends on, each drawn by the real view."""

    @classmethod
    def setUpTestData(cls):
        cache.clear()
        cls.html, cls.status = {}, {}

        def keep(state, response):
            cls.html[state] = response.content.decode()
            cls.status[state] = response.status_code

        def change(old=PASSWORD, new1=NEW_PASSWORD, new2=NEW_PASSWORD):
            return {"old_password": old, "new_password1": new1, "new_password2": new2}

        user = User.objects.create_user(username="pwpages", email="pwpages@example.com", password=PASSWORD)
        client = sign_in(user)
        keep("form", client.get(ADDRESS))
        keep("wrong old password", client.post(ADDRESS, change(old=WRONG_PASSWORD)))
        keep("mismatch", client.post(ADDRESS, change(new2=NEW_PASSWORD + "-other")))
        keep("too short", client.post(ADDRESS, change(new1="short1", new2="short1")))
        keep("done", client.post(ADDRESS, change(), follow=True))
        cache.clear()

    def states(self):
        """(state, the template's path for messages, the page's name, its HTML, its parsed tree) for each state."""
        return [(state, FILES + template, name, self.html[state], Tree(self.html[state])) for state, (template, name) in PAGES.items()]

    def test_every_state_answers_200(self):
        for state, status in self.status.items():
            with self.subTest(state=state):
                self.assertEqual(status, 200, f"{FILES}{PAGES[state][0]}: the '{state}' state answers {status}, not 200; the view keeps its status codes")

    def test_every_state_is_a_page_of_the_shell_on_the_form_layout_and_not_the_admins(self):
        for state, where, _name, page, _tree in self.states():
            with self.subTest(state=state):
                self.assertIn('<a class="skip-link label" href="#main">', page, f"{where}: extend layouts/form.html, which extends shell.html; the shell brings the skip link")
                self.assertRegex(page, r'<main id="main" class="shell-main">\s*<div class="form-page">', f"{where}: the page's words go in {{% block form_page %}} of layouts/form.html")
                self.assertRegex(page, r'<body class="[^"]*\blayout-form\b', f"{where}: the form layout gives the body the class layout-form")
                self.assertNotIn("data-layout", page, f"{where}: a form page has no registry layout, so it makes no in-place changes")
                for admin in ("Django administration", 'id="branding"', 'id="header"', "django-admin", "admin/css"):
                    self.assertNotIn(admin, page, f"{where}: found {admin!r}, which is the Django admin's page. Without a template of its own at templates/registration/ Django uses the admin's")

    def test_one_h1_inside_main_named_as_the_title(self):
        for state, where, name, page, tree in self.states():
            with self.subTest(state=state):
                h1s = tree.all("h1")
                self.assertEqual([words(h) for h in h1s], [name], f"{where}: one h1, the page's name, {name!r}")
                self.assertTrue(in_main(h1s[0]), f"{where}: the h1 belongs inside <main>")
                found = re.search(r"<title>(.*?)</title>", page, re.S).group(1)
                self.assertEqual(found, f"{name} | Veilfile", f"{where}: the title is {name!r} and ' | Veilfile' (no em dash), found {found!r}")
                for element in tree.elements:
                    if element["tag"] in ("header", "footer"):
                        self.assertFalse(in_main(element), f"{where}: no <{element['tag']}> inside <main>")

    def test_every_page_is_kept_out_of_search(self):
        for state, where, _name, page, _tree in self.states():
            with self.subTest(state=state):
                self.assertIn('<meta name="robots" content="noindex">', page, f'{where}: add {{% block meta %}}<meta name="robots" content="noindex">{{% endblock %}}; the page is a signed-in account page')

    def test_the_form_posts_to_its_own_address_with_its_own_csrf_token(self):
        for state in FORM_STATES:
            with self.subTest(state=state):
                tree = Tree(self.html[state])
                forms = tree.all("form")
                self.assertEqual(len(forms), 1, f"{FILES}{FORM}: one form, found {len(forms)}")
                self.assertEqual(forms[0]["attrs"].get("method"), "post")
                self.assertNotIn("action", forms[0]["attrs"], f"{FILES}{FORM}: no action attribute: the form posts to the address it came from")
                tokens = [e for e in tree.all("input") if inside(e, forms[0]) and e["attrs"].get("name") == "csrfmiddlewaretoken"]
                self.assertEqual(len(tokens), 1, f"{FILES}{FORM}: {{% csrf_token %}} goes in the page's own <form>, never in a component; found {len(tokens)}")
        self.assertEqual(Tree(self.html["done"]).all("form"), [], f"{FILES}{DONE}: the page it ends on has nothing to submit")

    def test_the_fields_keep_their_names_and_types_in_the_order_the_form_has_them(self):
        for state in FORM_STATES:
            with self.subTest(state=state):
                found = [(e["attrs"].get("name"), e["attrs"].get("type")) for e in Tree(self.html[state]).all("input") if e["attrs"].get("name") != "csrfmiddlewaretoken"]
                self.assertEqual(found, INPUTS, f"{FILES}{FORM}: the view's form reads these field names; found {found}")

    def test_every_input_has_one_visible_label_the_autocomplete_token_and_is_required(self):
        for state in FORM_STATES:
            with self.subTest(state=state):
                tree = Tree(self.html[state])
                for field in visible_inputs(tree):
                    name = field["attrs"]["id"]
                    labels = [label for label in tree.all("label") if label["attrs"].get("for") == name]
                    self.assertEqual(len(labels), 1, f"{FILES}{FORM}: the input {name!r} needs exactly one <label for>, found {len(labels)}")
                    self.assertTrue(words(labels[0]).startswith(LABELS[name]), f"{FILES}{FORM}: the label of {name} reads {LABELS[name]!r}, found {words(labels[0])!r}")
                    self.assertEqual(field["attrs"].get("autocomplete"), TOKENS[name], f"{FILES}{FORM}: {name} keeps autocomplete={TOKENS[name]!r} (password managers use them)")
                    self.assertIn("required", field["attrs"], f"{FILES}{FORM}: {name} is required")

    def test_the_new_password_field_shows_what_a_password_must_be(self):
        ids = Tree(self.html["form"]).ids()
        self.assertIn("id_new_password1_help", ids, f"{FILES}{FORM}: pass help=form.new_password1.help_text to the new password field")
        self.assertIn("at least 8 characters", words(ids["id_new_password1_help"]), f"{FILES}{FORM}: the help is the password validators' own rules")

    def test_a_field_error_is_tied_to_its_field_and_a_clean_field_is_not_marked(self):
        for state in FORM_STATES:
            with self.subTest(state=state):
                tree = Tree(self.html[state])
                ids = tree.ids()
                for element in tree.elements:
                    for token in element["attrs"].get("aria-describedby", "").split():
                        self.assertIn(token, ids, f"{FILES}{FORM}: aria-describedby names {token!r}, which is no id on the page")
                invalid = {e["attrs"]["id"]: e for e in visible_inputs(tree) if e["attrs"].get("aria-invalid") == "true"}
                wanted = ERRORS.get(state, {})
                self.assertEqual(set(invalid), set(wanted), f'{FILES}{FORM}: aria-invalid="true" belongs on the fields with an error ({sorted(wanted)}), found {sorted(invalid)}')
                for name, sentence in wanted.items():
                    described = " ".join(words(ids[token]) for token in invalid[name]["attrs"].get("aria-describedby", "").split())
                    self.assertIn(sentence, described, f"{FILES}{FORM}: the error under {name} reads {sentence!r} and aria-describedby must point at it; it points at {described!r}")

    def test_focus_goes_to_the_first_field_in_error_and_to_none_on_a_clean_form(self):
        wanted = {"form": [], "wrong old password": ["id_old_password"], "mismatch": ["id_new_password2"], "too short": ["id_new_password2"]}
        for state, ids in wanted.items():
            with self.subTest(state=state):
                focused = [e["attrs"].get("id") for e in Tree(self.html[state]).elements if "autofocus" in e["attrs"]]
                self.assertEqual(focused, ids, f"{FILES}{FORM}: {{% focus_field form \"old_password\" \"new_password1\" \"new_password2\" as focus %}} with no default (a page of several fields "
                                               f"takes none of its own), and focus=focus on each field; found {focused}")

    def test_a_typed_password_is_never_sent_back(self):
        for state in ("wrong old password", "mismatch", "too short"):
            for secret in (PASSWORD, NEW_PASSWORD, WRONG_PASSWORD, "short1"):
                with self.subTest(state=state, secret=secret):
                    self.assertNotIn(f'value="{secret}', self.html[state], f"{FILES}{FORM}: a password field never gets a value attribute")

    def test_the_words_the_buttons_and_the_links(self):
        for state in FORM_STATES:
            with self.subTest(state=state):
                tree = Tree(self.html[state])
                self.assertIn(INTRO, words(tree.all("main")[0]), f"{FILES}{FORM}: say what a change does; every part of it is true (tests_fix_auth holds the revoking, BehaviourTests below the sessions)")
                self.assertEqual([words(e) for e in tree.all("button") if in_main(e)], ["Change password"])
                links = [(words(e), e["attrs"].get("href"), e["attrs"].get("class")) for e in tree.all("a") if in_main(e)]
                self.assertEqual(links, [("Back to dashboard", "/app/", "label interactive")], f"{FILES}{FORM}: one quiet way back; found {links}")
                actions = [(e["tag"], e["attrs"]["class"]) for e in tree.elements if in_main(e) and "action" in e["attrs"].get("class", "").split()]
                self.assertEqual(actions, [("button", "action interactive")], f'{FILES}{FORM}: the one main action is <button class="action interactive" type="submit">; found {actions}')
        done = Tree(self.html["done"])
        self.assertIn(DONE_WORDS, words(done.all("main")[0]), f"{FILES}{DONE}: keep the sentence {DONE_WORDS!r}")
        links = [(words(e), e["attrs"].get("href"), e["attrs"].get("class")) for e in done.all("a") if in_main(e)]
        self.assertEqual(links, [("Go to dashboard", "/app/", "action interactive")], f"{FILES}{DONE}: the next step is the main action; found {links}")

    def test_the_templates_keep_the_voice(self):
        for template in (FORM, DONE):
            text = (Path(settings.BASE_DIR) / "templates" / "registration" / template).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            words_only = re.sub(r"{%.*?%}|{#.*?#}|{{.*?}}", "", text)  # a template tag may say != ; the words may not shout
            with self.subTest(template=template):
                self.assertNotIn("\N{EM DASH}", text, f"{FILES}{template}: no em dashes; use a colon, a comma or two sentences")
                self.assertNotIn("!", words_only, f"{FILES}{template}: no exclamation marks")
                for word in BANNED:
                    self.assertNotIn(word, text.lower(), f"{FILES}{template}: avoid {word.strip()!r} (AGENTS.md, voice)")

    def test_the_menu_is_the_signed_in_menu_of_the_site(self):
        for state in ("form", "done"):
            with self.subTest(state=state):
                self.assertIn('href="/app/">Dashboard</a>', self.html[state], f"{FILES}{PAGES[state][0]}: the shell's menu offers the Dashboard to a signed-in visitor")
                self.assertNotIn(">Sign in</a>", self.html[state])


class FormErrorsTests(PageTestCase):
    """An error of the form itself, which belongs to no field, is an alert, and it has focus when no field is in error."""

    def render(self, form):
        request = RequestFactory().get(ADDRESS)
        request.user = AnonymousUser()
        return render_to_string("registration/" + FORM, {"form": form}, request=request)

    def test_a_non_field_error_is_shown_in_an_alert_that_takes_focus(self):
        sentence = "This is an error of the form itself."
        owner = User.objects.create_user(username="pwalert", email="pwalert@example.com", password=PASSWORD)
        form = PasswordChangeForm(owner, {"old_password": PASSWORD, "new_password1": NEW_PASSWORD, "new_password2": NEW_PASSWORD})
        self.assertTrue(form.is_valid())
        form.add_error(None, sentence)
        tree = Tree(self.render(form))
        alerts = tree.announced("alert")
        self.assertEqual([a for a in alerts if sentence in a], [f"Check this {sentence}"],
                         f"{FILES}{FORM}: show {{% include \"components/form_errors.html\" with errors=form.non_field_errors focus=summary only %}} above the form; the alerts found are {alerts}")
        focused = [e["attrs"].get("id") or ("alert" if e["attrs"].get("role") == "alert" else e["tag"]) for e in tree.elements if "autofocus" in e["attrs"]]
        self.assertEqual(focused, ["alert"], f"{FILES}{FORM}: with only an error of its own the summary takes focus ({{% focus_summary %}}) and no field does; found {focused}")

    def test_a_field_in_error_takes_focus_before_the_summary(self):
        owner = User.objects.create_user(username="pwboth", email="pwboth@example.com", password=PASSWORD)
        form = PasswordChangeForm(owner, {"old_password": PASSWORD, "new_password1": NEW_PASSWORD, "new_password2": NEW_PASSWORD})
        self.assertTrue(form.is_valid())
        form.add_error(None, "This is an error of the form itself.")
        form.add_error("new_password2", "This field has its own error.")
        focused = [e["attrs"].get("id") or e["tag"] for e in Tree(self.render(form)).elements if "autofocus" in e["attrs"]]
        self.assertEqual(focused, ["id_new_password2"], f"{FILES}{FORM}: one autofocus on the page, the field in error; found {focused}")


class BehaviourTests(PageTestCase):
    """What the view does has not changed with the page."""

    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        self.user = User.objects.create_user(username="pwbehave", email="pwbehave@example.com", password=PASSWORD)

    def test_a_signed_out_visitor_is_sent_to_log_in_and_back(self):
        for address in (ADDRESS, DONE_ADDRESS):
            with self.subTest(address=address):
                response = Client().get(address)
                self.assertEqual((response.status_code, response["Location"]), (302, f"/accounts/login/?next={address}"), "the pages need a session, as they did")

    def test_a_good_change_goes_to_the_done_page_and_sets_the_password(self):
        client = sign_in(self.user)
        response = client.post(ADDRESS, {"old_password": PASSWORD, "new_password1": NEW_PASSWORD, "new_password2": NEW_PASSWORD})
        self.assertEqual((response.status_code, response["Location"]), (302, DONE_ADDRESS))
        self.user.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertTrue(self.user.check_password(NEW_PASSWORD))
        self.assertEqual(client.get(DONE_ADDRESS).status_code, 200)

    def test_the_session_that_changes_the_password_stays_and_the_others_are_signed_out(self):
        # The intro and the done page say so: "signs out your other sessions" is what Django's PasswordChangeView does (update_session_auth_hash).
        here, elsewhere = sign_in(self.user), sign_in(self.user)
        self.assertEqual(elsewhere.get(ADDRESS).status_code, 200)
        here.post(ADDRESS, {"old_password": PASSWORD, "new_password1": NEW_PASSWORD, "new_password2": NEW_PASSWORD})
        self.assertEqual(here.get(ADDRESS).status_code, 200, "the session that changed it is still signed in")
        self.assertEqual(elsewhere.get(ADDRESS).status_code, 302, "another session of the same user is signed out by the change")

    def test_a_wrong_old_password_changes_nothing(self):
        client = sign_in(self.user)
        response = client.post(ADDRESS, {"old_password": WRONG_PASSWORD, "new_password1": NEW_PASSWORD, "new_password2": NEW_PASSWORD})
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.user.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertTrue(self.user.check_password(PASSWORD))
```

### Task 4: Files

The Files section is two pages. `GET /app/files/` lists the signed-in user's files, 50 to a page, newest first. Each row shows its name, size, when it was added and when it expires, its secret flags in words, its state (live, expired or held) and, while its link works, Copy and Revoke. `/app/files/<uuid>/revoke/` is the confirmation page: a GET shows it and changes nothing, and a POST revokes the file and goes back to the list with one line. Both are Django views over Task 1's account functions, on Task 2's app layout and its stacked-rows table. The list itself is a new component, `file_list`.

Three choices here are the owner's to overrule, each with its reason in the notes below: Copy keeps the site's one word, "Copy"; only a live file is offered Revoke, and a file that is not live is sent back to the list with a sentence if its address is opened; and `copy.js` does not change.

- Modify (replaced whole): `backend/templates/dashboard/files.html` (Task 2's stub)
- Modify: `backend/templates/shell.html` (one stylesheet link), `backend/pages/catalog.py` (the component's entry)

Notes for an engineer new to the repo, and the decisions this task makes:

- **The list is a component, and its stylesheet is the shell's.**
  - An in-place change (`shell.js`) swaps `<main>` and the marked `<head>` elements, and brings no stylesheet. The five sections are one family, so a visitor reaches Files from Overview in place, and rules in a `{% block styles %}` of the Files page would be missing.
  - The rules are therefore a component's (`static/css/components/file_list.css`), linked from `shell.html` like every component's. The component also gets what the recipe asks of one: a catalog entry that shows the list in its states (the 512-character name too) and a rendering test.
  - A test fails a `styles` block in either page.
- **How a row tells its state.**
  - The endpoint's rows (the API's, which clients read, so they stay as they are) carry `expires_at` and not `safety_status`.
  - `state_of` is "expired" once `expires_at` is not after now, held or not (the endpoint lists expired rows until the sweep deletes them, and a revoke whose storage delete failed keeps one), else "held", else "live".
  - "Held" comes from one extra query for the ids on the page, within the user's own workspace (`held_ids`). A held file's link answers like a missing one (`serve_artifact`), so the page offers nothing for it.
  - Only a live row carries its link in the page: the others' open nothing.
- **Copy, and the one status.**
  - `copy.js` reads `document.getElementById(button.dataset.copy)`, takes the text of `[data-copy-text]` inside it or of the element itself, and says "Copied" in the first `[data-copy-status]` inside the button's nearest `[data-tabs]` or `[data-code-block]`, else in the document's first.
  - A live row therefore holds its link in `<code class="visually-hidden" id="file-url-<uuid>" aria-hidden="true">` in its Actions cell, its button names that id, and the list has one status line for all its rows. Copy finds it through the document, and `copy.js` stays as it is: `shell.js` plus the behaviours remain at the 9,586 B gzipped that Task 2's `local-time.js` (474 B) brought them to (9,112 B on main), of the 10,240 B budget: 654 B free. A test pins the line of `copy.js` that the markup relies on, and one that the list has exactly one status and no `data-tabs` or `data-code-block` around a row.
  - A status for each row and a `[data-copy-scope]` selector would cost bytes and a changed pin for nothing: a live region is read wherever it is.
  - The link is visually hidden and not `hidden`: when the clipboard refuses, `copy.js` selects the text and says "Selected", and a `display: none` element cannot be selected, so Ctrl+C would copy nothing. It is hidden from screen readers (fifty links of about 66 characters would be read out) and never shown: the React dashboard only copied it, and a bearer link on screen is one that a screen share leaks. It is in the page's markup for live files only, as it was in the JSON, so the page is `never_cache`d.
  - The visible word is "Copy", not React's "Copy URL". `copy.js` puts the label back as "Copy" after 1.8 s, and "Copy" is what the install line and every code block say. The accessible name is "Copy link for NAME": it starts with the visible word (WCAG 2.5.3) and says whose link.
- **Which rows get which controls.** A live row has Copy and Revoke. An expired or held row has neither (its Actions cell says "None") and is set in `--muted`.
- **Revoke.**
  - Revoke is a link to the confirmation page, so a GET never revokes. The page names the file, has one POST button and a "Keep it" link back to Files, and its form posts to its own address with `{% csrf_token %}` in it.
  - **Ownership.** The file is looked up in the user's workspace, `Artifact.objects.filter(id=..., workspace=get_or_create_workspace(user))`: the workspace the list and `account.revoke_artifact` read, so the page, the confirmation and the revoke agree on which files are the user's (a user who somehow owns two workspaces sees and revokes the oldest one's files only). Another user's file and a missing one are the same shell 404, for a GET and a POST, with the same bytes (a test compares them) whether the file is live, expired or held: the ownership check comes before the state check, so the "not live" sentence never tells a stranger that an id exists. A malformed id never reaches the view (`<uuid:artifact_id>`). A user who has no workspace yet is given one, as the Files list and the JSON endpoints give it on a first visit.
  - **A file that is not live** is not revoked here, for a GET or a POST: Review Focus 2 asks for a 404 or a sentence and never a change. The visitor goes back to Files with `NOT_LIVE`, "That file's link has already stopped working, so there is nothing to revoke." (it names neither state, because it covers expired and held). It also covers a file that expired while the confirmation page was open. A held file is the safety review's to release, and an expired one is deleted by the sweep.
  - **A storage failure.** `services.revoke_artifact` turns every storage failure into one case, `REVOKE_PENDING_DELETE`: the link is already dead, the row is kept (expired) and the sweep deletes the file later. The account function answers 204 for it with `{"storage_deleted": False}`, so the view reads the case from that flag and says `REVOKED_PENDING` instead of claiming the file is gone. That is the one sentence for "REVOKE_PENDING_DELETE" and for "a storage failure". The kept row shows as Expired with no controls, so the dashboard cannot retry it; the sweep does (daily, and lazily on uploads), and the API and MCP can still revoke it.
  - **Messages.** `messages.success`, `warning` and `info` carry fixed sentences. Nothing of the file (its name, its link) goes into a message, which is kept in the session or a cookie.
  - **A resent POST** (a reload after the redirect) finds no file and is the shell 404, as the spec's missing id is.
- **Pagination.**
  - `FILES_PER_PAGE` is 50. "Older files" links `?cursor=<X-Next-Cursor>` (`rel="next"`) and "Newest" goes back to `/app/files/` whenever the address carries a good cursor. The path is in the family's `layout_paths`, so both change in place (`shell.js` compares paths, not queries).
  - A `?cursor=` the endpoint rejects (it answers 400 `invalid_request`) shows page one with "That link to older files is not valid. Here are your newest files." and status 200: a link someone mistyped or cut short should not end at an error page. An empty `?cursor=` is page one with no sentence.
  - A valid cursor is a position, not a pass: the list filters on the signed-in user's workspace first, and a test sends one user's cursor as another.
- **Caching.** `@never_cache`: the page holds live links, which are credentials (invariant 1 says never to log them; a stored copy of the page is the same exposure).
- **Words.**
  - Kept from the React dashboard: the empty-state sentence ("No artifacts yet. Create a key above, point your agent at its variable name, and uploads will appear here." becomes "No files yet. Create a key under Keys, point your agent at its variable name, and uploads will appear here.") and the confirm question ("Revoke this artifact? Its URL stops working." becomes "Revoke this file?" and "Its link stops working at once and the file is deleted. This cannot be undone.").
  - New, in the voice rules (no em dashes, no exclamation marks, none of the banned words; ASCII only):
    - the page's lead ("What your agents have pushed, newest first. A secret flag means the scan found text shaped like a secret: the link still works until the file expires or you revoke it. The link of an expired or held file no longer opens."; the second sentence restates `docs/llms.txt`: a flagged upload is stored and its link works);
    - the flags in words (below);
    - the three message sentences;
    - the bad-cursor sentence;
    - "There are no older files.";
    - the table's caption.
  - The scanner's flag names read as: `github_pat` and `github_token` "GitHub token", `openai_key` "OpenAI key", `anthropic_key` "Anthropic key", `stripe_key` "Stripe key", `aws_access_key` "AWS access key", `aws_secret_key` "AWS secret key", `private_key` "Private key", `slack_token` "Slack token", `google_api_key` "Google API key", `generic_secret` "Password or secret". A test keeps the table as long as `drop_core/secrets.py`'s list.
- **What the controller must check against Task 2's final text** (Step 1 does): the name of the `files` stub, the library the two filters are in (`dashboard`), the text of the `app-files` route and registry lines this task adds to, and what `layouts/app.html` draws for a message. The tests read these through the rendered page, so a mismatch fails with a message that names the file.

```python
"""The Files section of the dashboard (spec 4.8): the list and its pager, the Copy and Revoke each live row offers, and the
confirmation page that revokes a file.

Every class sets longMessage = False, so that a failure prints its own message, which names the file and the fix, and not the
page it searched.
"""
import io
import re
from contextlib import contextmanager
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone as dt_timezone
from html import unescape
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock
from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlsplit

from django.conf import settings
from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.core.management import call_command
from django.template.loader import render_to_string
from django.test import Client, SimpleTestCase, TestCase
from django.urls import reverse
from django.utils import timezone

from dashboard import views as dashboard_views
from dashboard.file_rows import FLAG_WORDS, file_rows, flag_words, held_ids, state_of
from drop_core import account, secrets
from drop_core.models import Artifact, Workspace, get_or_create_workspace
from drop_core.storage import LocalStorage
from pages import catalog, tests_forms_on_the_shell
from pages.tests_chapters import BANNED
from pages.tests_reading import declarations

User = get_user_model()
PASSWORD = "pw12345678"
BACKEND = Path(settings.BASE_DIR)
TEMPLATES = BACKEND / "templates"
STATIC = BACKEND / "static"
OWN_TEMPLATES = ("components/file_list.html", "dashboard/files.html", "dashboard/file_revoke.html")
LABELS = ["File", "Size", "Added", "Expires", "Secret flags", "State", "Actions"]
LIST = "/app/files/"
ROW = re.compile(r'<tr class="files__row" data-state="([^"]+)">(.*?)</tr>', re.S)
CELL = re.compile(r'<td[^>]*?data-label="([^"]+)"[^>]*>(.*?)</td>', re.S)
HOSTILE = '"><img src=x onerror=alert(1)><script>alert(2)</script>'


def text_of(fragment):
    """The words a reader sees in a piece of markup."""
    return " ".join(unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", fragment)).split())


def rows_in(html):
    """Each file row of a page or a component, in order: its state, its cells' words by label, their markup by label, its markup."""
    found = []
    for state, markup in ROW.findall(html):
        cells = CELL.findall(markup)
        found.append({"state": state, "markup": markup, "html": dict(cells),
                      "cells": {label: text_of(cell) for label, cell in cells}})
    return found


def notices(html):
    """The words of each element with class notice and role status on a page, whatever its tag."""
    found = []
    for opening in re.finditer(r"<(\w+)\b([^>]*)>", html):
        tag, attrs = opening.groups()
        if re.search(r'class="[^"]*\bnotice\b', attrs) and 'role="status"' in attrs:
            found.append(text_of(html[opening.end():html.index(f"</{tag}>", opening.end())]))
    return found


def links_in(html):
    """[(attributes text, words)] of each <a> in a piece of markup."""
    return [(attrs, text_of(body)) for attrs, body in re.findall(r"<a\b([^>]*)>(.*?)</a>", html, re.S)]


def href_of(html, words):
    """The href of the first link whose words are `words`, or None."""
    for attrs, text in links_in(html):
        if text == words:
            return re.search(r'href="([^"]*)"', attrs).group(1)
    return None


def main_of(html):
    return html[html.index("<main"):html.index("</main>")]


def without_tokens(html):
    """A page with its CSRF token values blanked: Django masks a token differently on every render."""
    return re.sub(r'(name="csrfmiddlewaretoken" value=")[^"]*', r"\1", html)


class FailingDeleteStorage(LocalStorage):
    """A storage whose delete fails, as R2 does in an outage."""

    def delete(self, token):
        raise ConnectionError(f"R2 503 for https://r2.example/bucket/{token}")


class FilesCase(TestCase):
    """A signed-in owner with a workspace, and the means to give it files that have bytes in storage."""
    longMessage = False

    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        self.owner = User.objects.create_user("owner", email="owner@example.com", password=PASSWORD)
        self.workspace = get_or_create_workspace(self.owner)
        self.client.force_login(self.owner)

    def make_file(self, name="report.pdf", *, workspace=None, size=1500, days=7, flags=(), held=False, created=None, data=b"bytes"):
        """A file of `workspace` (the owner's by default) with its bytes in storage; `days` before it expires, negative once it has."""
        artifact = Artifact.objects.create(
            workspace=workspace or self.workspace, filename=name, size_bytes=size, expires_at=timezone.now() + timedelta(days=days),
            secret_flags=list(flags), safety_status="held" if held else "clear")
        LocalStorage().save(artifact.token, io.BytesIO(data), "application/octet-stream")
        self.addCleanup(LocalStorage().delete, artifact.token)
        if created is not None:
            Artifact.objects.filter(pk=artifact.pk).update(created_at=created)
            artifact.refresh_from_db()
        return artifact

    def stored(self, artifact):
        return LocalStorage().exists(artifact.token)

    @contextmanager
    def storage_down(self):
        """Every storage delete fails, as in an outage; the error the revoke logs for it is expected."""
        with mock.patch("drop_core.services.get_storage", return_value=FailingDeleteStorage()), \
                self.assertLogs("drop_core.services", "ERROR"):
            yield

    def link_status(self, artifact):
        """What the public link of a file answers a stranger."""
        response = Client().get(f"/a/{artifact.token}")
        response.close()
        return response.status_code

    def other_user(self, name="other"):
        user = User.objects.create_user(name, email=f"{name}@example.com", password=PASSWORD)
        return user, get_or_create_workspace(user)

    def revoke_url(self, artifact):
        return reverse("app-file-revoke", args=[artifact.id])


class FileRowsTests(FilesCase):
    """dashboard/file_rows.py: the list endpoint's rows with a state and flags in words."""

    def rows(self):
        body = account.list_artifacts(self.owner, limit=50).body
        return {row["name"]: row for row in file_rows(self.owner, body)}

    def test_every_scanner_flag_has_words(self):
        names = {name for name, _pattern, _check in secrets._PATTERNS}
        self.assertEqual(set(FLAG_WORDS), names,
                         "backend/dashboard/file_rows.py: FLAG_WORDS needs the words for each flag backend/drop_core/secrets.py can report, and for no other")

    def test_flags_are_said_in_words_once_each_in_the_order_reported(self):
        self.assertEqual(flag_words(["github_pat", "github_token", "stripe_key"]), ["GitHub token", "Stripe key"],
                         "backend/dashboard/file_rows.py: two flags that read the same are said once")
        self.assertEqual(flag_words(["aws_access_key", "generic_secret"]), ["AWS access key", "Password or secret"])
        self.assertEqual(flag_words([]), [])
        self.assertEqual(flag_words(None), [])

    def test_a_flag_the_table_lacks_is_still_readable(self):
        self.assertEqual(flag_words(["brand_new_thing"]), ["Brand new thing"],
                         "backend/dashboard/file_rows.py: an unknown flag reads as its name without underscores, never as a raw identifier")

    def test_a_row_is_live_expired_or_held(self):
        self.make_file("live.txt")
        self.make_file("old.txt", days=-1)
        self.make_file("held.txt", held=True)
        self.make_file("held-and-old.txt", held=True, days=-1)
        states = {name: row["state"] for name, row in self.rows().items()}
        self.assertEqual(states, {"live.txt": "live", "old.txt": "expired", "held.txt": "held", "held-and-old.txt": "expired"},
                         "backend/dashboard/file_rows.py: expired once expires_at has passed (held or not), else held, else live")

    def test_the_state_rule(self):
        now = datetime(2026, 10, 22, 12, 0, tzinfo=dt_timezone.utc)
        later, earlier = now + timedelta(seconds=1), now - timedelta(seconds=1)
        self.assertEqual([state_of(later, False, now), state_of(later, True, now), state_of(earlier, False, now), state_of(earlier, True, now),
                          state_of(now, False, now)],
                         ["live", "held", "expired", "expired", "expired"],
                         "backend/dashboard/file_rows.py: state_of: expired once expires_at is not after now (held or not), else held, else live")

    def test_only_a_live_row_carries_its_link(self):
        self.make_file("live.txt")
        self.make_file("old.txt", days=-1)
        self.make_file("held.txt", held=True)
        listed = {item["filename"]: item["url"] for item in account.list_artifacts(self.owner, limit=50).body}
        for name, row in self.rows().items():
            with self.subTest(file=name):
                self.assertEqual(row["url"], listed[name] if row["state"] == "live" else "",
                                 "backend/dashboard/file_rows.py: the url of a row that is not live stays out of the page; its link opens nothing")

    def test_a_row_keeps_what_the_endpoint_said(self):
        artifact = self.make_file("kept.txt", size=2048, flags=["private_key"], days=3)
        row = self.rows()["kept.txt"]
        self.assertEqual((row["id"], row["size"], row["flags"]), (str(artifact.id), 2048, ["Private key"]))
        self.assertEqual((row["added"], row["expires"]), (artifact.created_at, artifact.expires_at))
        self.assertIsNotNone(row["added"].tzinfo, "backend/dashboard/file_rows.py: times are aware, so utc_time can write them in UTC")

    def test_held_is_looked_for_among_the_owners_own_files_only(self):
        _other, other_workspace = self.other_user()
        theirs = self.make_file("theirs.txt", workspace=other_workspace, held=True)
        mine = self.make_file("mine.txt", held=True)
        self.assertEqual(held_ids(self.owner, [{"id": str(theirs.id)}, {"id": str(mine.id)}]), {str(mine.id)},
                         "backend/dashboard/file_rows.py: held_ids asks within the signed-in user's own workspace")
        self.assertEqual(held_ids(self.owner, []), set())


def sample(number, name="report.pdf", *, state="live", size=3400, flags=(), days=7):
    """A row as file_rows makes it, for the component."""
    added = datetime(2026, 10, 22, 13, 58, tzinfo=dt_timezone.utc)
    return {"id": f"00000000-0000-4000-8000-{number:012d}", "name": name, "size": size, "added": added,
            "expires": added + timedelta(days=days), "flags": list(flags), "state": state,
            "url": f"https://veilfile.com/a/sample-{number}" if state == "live" else ""}


def render_list(files, **inputs):
    context = {"files": files, "id_prefix": "t", "older_url": "", "newest_url": "", **inputs}
    return render_to_string("components/file_list.html", context)


class FileListComponentTests(SimpleTestCase):
    """components/file_list.html: what it draws for the rows it is given."""
    longMessage = False
    FILE = "backend/templates/components/file_list.html"

    def five(self):
        return [sample(1, "release-notes.md"), sample(2, "deploy.env", size=912, flags=["Stripe key", "Password or secret"]),
                sample(3, "screenshots.zip", state="expired", size=48_300_000, days=-1),
                sample(4, "export.csv", state="held", size=2_150_000_000), sample(5, "x" * 508 + ".txt")]

    def test_a_table_of_stacked_rows_with_a_caption_and_scoped_column_headers(self):
        html = render_list(self.five())
        self.assertEqual(html.count("<table"), 1)
        self.assertIn('<table class="rows files">', html, f"{self.FILE}: the list is the dashboard's stacked-rows table, <table class=\"rows\">")
        self.assertRegex(html, r"<caption>[^<]+</caption>", f"{self.FILE}: a table has a caption (spec 9)")
        headers = re.findall(r'<th scope="col">(.*?)</th>', html, re.S)
        self.assertEqual([text_of(header) for header in headers], LABELS,
                         f"{self.FILE}: seven column headers with scope=\"col\"; the last, for the controls, is visually hidden")
        self.assertEqual(len(re.findall(r"<th\b", html)), 7)
        self.assertIn('<th scope="col"><span class="visually-hidden">Actions</span></th>', html)

    def test_every_cell_keeps_its_label_in_every_row(self):
        rows = rows_in(render_list(self.five()))
        self.assertEqual(len(rows), 5)
        for row in rows:
            with self.subTest(file=row["cells"].get("File", "")[:12]):
                self.assertEqual(list(row["cells"]), LABELS,
                                 f"{self.FILE}: each <td> carries data-label, so a phone's stacked row keeps the name of every value (spec 4.10)")

    def test_a_name_is_escaped_in_its_cell_and_in_the_names_of_its_controls(self):
        html = render_list([sample(1, HOSTILE)])
        self.assertNotIn("<img", html, f"{self.FILE}: {{{{ file.name }}}} is escaped wherever it is written")
        self.assertNotIn("<script", html)
        self.assertEqual(rows_in(html)[0]["cells"]["File"], HOSTILE)
        for control in re.findall(r'aria-label="([^"]*)"', html):
            self.assertIn("&quot;", control, f"{self.FILE}: the file's name is escaped in aria-label too")

    def test_the_whole_of_a_long_name_is_in_the_cell(self):
        name = "x" * 508 + ".txt"
        self.assertEqual(len(name), 512)
        self.assertEqual(rows_in(render_list([sample(1, name)]))[0]["cells"]["File"], name)

    def test_times_are_written_for_the_visitors_zone(self):
        row = rows_in(render_list([sample(1)]))[0]
        self.assertIn('<time datetime="2026-10-22T13:58Z" data-local>', row["html"]["Added"],
                      f"{self.FILE}: Added goes through |utc_time, which writes <time datetime data-local> in UTC for behaviors/local-time.js")
        self.assertIn('<time datetime="2026-10-29T13:58Z" data-local>', row["html"]["Expires"])
        self.assertIn("UTC", row["cells"]["Added"], "with no script the reader still sees the time, and the zone it is in")

    def test_sizes_go_through_the_bytes_filter(self):
        sizes = [row["cells"]["Size"] for row in rows_in(render_list(self.five()))]
        self.assertEqual(sizes, ["3.3 KB", "912 B", "46.1 MB", "2.0 GB", "3.3 KB"], f"{self.FILE}: Size is {{{{ file.size|bytes }}}}")

    def test_secret_flags_are_words_or_none(self):
        flags = [row["cells"]["Secret flags"] for row in rows_in(render_list(self.five()))]
        self.assertEqual(flags, ["None", "Stripe key, Password or secret", "None", "None", "None"])

    def test_the_state_is_a_word_in_its_cell_and_on_its_row(self):
        rows = rows_in(render_list(self.five()))
        self.assertEqual([(row["state"], row["cells"]["State"]) for row in rows],
                         [("live", "Live"), ("live", "Live"), ("expired", "Expired"), ("held", "Held"), ("live", "Live")],
                         f"{self.FILE}: data-state on the row is the state's key (the stylesheet and the browser checks read it); the cell says it in a word")

    def test_only_a_live_row_has_copy_and_revoke(self):
        rows = rows_in(render_list(self.five()))
        for row in rows:
            with self.subTest(state=row["state"], file=row["cells"]["File"][:12]):
                actions = row["html"]["Actions"]
                if row["state"] == "live":
                    self.assertEqual(len(re.findall(r"<button\b", actions)), 1)
                    self.assertEqual([text for _attrs, text in links_in(actions)], ["Revoke"])
                else:
                    self.assertEqual(row["cells"]["Actions"], "None")
                    self.assertNotIn("<button", actions)
                    self.assertNotIn("<a ", actions, f"{self.FILE}: a file whose link has stopped working offers neither Copy nor Revoke")

    def test_copy_reads_the_link_in_its_own_row(self):
        for row in rows_in(render_list(self.five())):
            if row["state"] != "live":
                continue
            actions = row["html"]["Actions"]
            target = re.search(r'<button class="files__copy label interactive" type="button" data-copy="([^"]+)"', actions).group(1)
            holder = re.search(rf'<code class="visually-hidden" id="{re.escape(target)}" aria-hidden="true">([^<]*)</code>', actions)
            with self.subTest(target=target):
                self.assertIsNotNone(holder, f"{self.FILE}: the button's data-copy names a <code> with that id in the same cell, which copy.js reads")
                self.assertRegex(holder.group(1), r"^https://veilfile\.com/a/sample-\d$")
        html = render_list(self.five())
        ids = re.findall(r'\sid="([^"]+)"', html)
        self.assertEqual(len(ids), len(set(ids)), f"{self.FILE}: every id on the list is unique")
        self.assertTrue(all(found.startswith("t-url-") for found in ids), f"{self.FILE}: ids are made from the id_prefix input")

    def test_copy_is_named_by_its_file_and_keeps_the_visible_word(self):
        html = render_list([sample(1, "plans.pdf")])
        self.assertIn('aria-label="Copy link for plans.pdf">Copy</button>', html,
                      f"{self.FILE}: Copy's name says whose link it copies and starts with the visible word (WCAG 2.5.3)")
        self.assertIn('aria-label="Revoke plans.pdf">Revoke</a>', html)

    def test_the_link_is_hidden_from_a_screen_reader_and_never_a_link_to_open(self):
        html = render_list(self.five())
        self.assertEqual(html.count("https://veilfile.com/a/"), 3, "only live rows write their link, once each")
        self.assertNotIn('href="https://veilfile.com/a/', html, f"{self.FILE}: a file's link is copied, never offered as a link to open")

    def test_copy_speaks_in_the_one_status_of_the_page(self):
        html = render_list(self.five())
        self.assertEqual(html.count("data-copy-status"), 1,
                         f"{self.FILE}: copy.js falls back to the first [data-copy-status] in the document, so the list has one status for all its rows")
        self.assertIn('<p class="visually-hidden" role="status" data-copy-status></p>', html)
        for scope in ("data-tabs", "data-code-block"):
            self.assertNotIn(scope, html, f"{self.FILE}: copy.js looks for the nearest [data-tabs] or [data-code-block] first; a row inside one would speak there")

    def test_copy_js_falls_back_to_the_document_for_its_status(self):
        script = (STATIC / "js/behaviors/copy.js").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertIn('button.closest("[data-tabs], [data-code-block]") || document', script,
                      "backend/static/js/behaviors/copy.js: the Files list has one status and no block around its rows, so Copy must still look in the document; "
                      "change the list's markup together with this line")

    def test_revoke_goes_to_the_confirmation_page_of_its_file(self):
        html = render_list([sample(7, "a.txt")])
        self.assertEqual(href_of(html, "Revoke"), "/app/files/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000007/revoke/",
                         f"{self.FILE}: Revoke is a link to {{% url 'app-file-revoke' file.id %}}; a GET never revokes")
        self.assertNotIn("<form", html, f"{self.FILE}: the list holds no form; revoking is a POST from the confirmation page")

    def test_the_pager_offers_only_the_ways_that_exist(self):
        files = [sample(1)]
        for older, newest, expected in (("", "", []), ("/app/files/?cursor=1-2", "", ["Older files"]), ("", "/app/files/", ["Newest"]),
                                        ("/app/files/?cursor=1-2", "/app/files/", ["Newest", "Older files"])):
            with self.subTest(older=older, newest=newest):
                html = render_list(files, older_url=older, newest_url=newest)
                found = re.findall(r'<nav class="files__pager" aria-label="More files">(.*?)</nav>', html, re.S)
                self.assertEqual([text for _attrs, text in links_in(found[0])] if found else [], expected)
                if older:
                    self.assertEqual(href_of(html, "Older files"), older)
                    self.assertIn('rel="next"', html)
                if newest:
                    self.assertEqual(href_of(html, "Newest"), newest)

    def test_no_files_says_so_and_points_to_keys(self):
        html = render_list([])
        self.assertNotIn("<table", html, f"{self.FILE}: an empty list is words, not a table with no rows")
        self.assertIn("No files yet. Create a key under Keys, point your agent at its variable name, and uploads will appear here.", html)
        self.assertEqual(href_of(html, "Go to Keys"), "/app/keys/")

    def test_a_page_past_the_oldest_file_says_so_and_offers_the_way_back(self):
        html = render_list([], newest_url="/app/files/")
        self.assertIn("There are no older files.", html)
        self.assertNotIn("No files yet", html)
        self.assertEqual(href_of(html, "Newest"), "/app/files/")

    def test_a_rows_controls_are_buttons_and_links_that_answer_the_cursor(self):
        html = render_list([sample(1)], older_url="/app/files/?cursor=1-2", newest_url="/app/files/")
        for tag in re.findall(r"<(?:button|a)\b[^>]*>", html):
            self.assertIn("interactive", tag, f"{self.FILE}: {tag} needs the class interactive, which gives a control the ink wash on hover and a press")


class FilesPageTests(FilesCase):
    """GET /app/files/."""

    def test_the_addresses_are_the_ones_the_menu_and_the_links_use(self):
        self.assertEqual(reverse("app-files"), LIST)
        self.assertEqual(reverse("app-file-revoke", args=["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]),
                         "/app/files/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001/revoke/",
                         "backend/dashboard/urls.py: app-files is /app/files/ and app-file-revoke is /app/files/<uuid:artifact_id>/revoke/")

    def test_signed_out_goes_to_sign_in_and_back(self):
        response = Client().get(LIST)
        self.assertEqual((response.status_code, response["Location"]), (302, "/accounts/login/?next=/app/files/"),
                         "backend/dashboard/views.py: files is wrapped in @dashboard_view, which needs a signed-in user")

    def test_the_page_is_files_on_the_app_layout(self):
        response = self.client.get(LIST)
        html = response.content.decode()
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertIn("<title>Files | Veilfile</title>", html, "backend/pages/context_processors.py: the entry for app-files has the title Files | Veilfile")
        self.assertEqual(re.findall(r"<h1[^>]*>(.*?)</h1>", main_of(html), re.S), ["Files"], "backend/templates/dashboard/files.html: one h1, Files, inside <main>")
        self.assertRegex(html, r'<body class="[^"]*\blayout-app\b', "backend/templates/dashboard/files.html extends layouts/app.html")
        self.assertIn('data-layout="app"', html, "the five sections are one layout family (backend/pages/context_processors.py), so moving among them is in place")
        self.assertEqual(response["X-Robots-Tag"], "noindex, nofollow")
        self.assertIn('<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">', html, "backend/templates/layouts/app.html: the meta block carries noindex, nofollow")

    def test_the_page_is_never_cached_because_it_holds_bearer_links(self):
        self.make_file()
        cache_control = self.client.get(LIST)["Cache-Control"]
        self.assertIn("no-store", cache_control, "backend/dashboard/views.py: files carries @never_cache; a live file's link is a bearer credential")

    def test_the_list_holds_no_form_because_every_action_is_a_page_of_its_own(self):
        self.make_file()
        html = main_of(self.client.get(LIST).content.decode())
        self.assertNotIn("<form", html, "backend/templates/components/file_list.html: Revoke is a link to its confirmation page; a GET never changes anything")
        self.assertNotIn("csrfmiddlewaretoken", html)

    def test_the_page_shows_what_the_endpoint_lists_in_its_order(self):
        for number in range(4):
            self.make_file(f"f{number}.txt", created=timezone.now() - timedelta(hours=number))
        body = account.list_artifacts(self.owner, limit=50).body
        rows = rows_in(self.client.get(LIST).content.decode())
        self.assertEqual([row["cells"]["File"] for row in rows], [item["filename"] for item in body])
        self.assertEqual(re.findall(r"/app/files/([0-9a-f-]{36})/revoke/", main_of(self.client.get(LIST).content.decode())), [item["id"] for item in body])

    def test_it_lists_the_owners_files_newest_first_with_their_words(self):
        base = timezone.now() - timedelta(hours=3)
        self.make_file("first.txt", size=100, created=base)
        self.make_file("second.txt", size=2048, flags=["stripe_key"], created=base + timedelta(hours=1))
        self.make_file("gone.zip", size=3 * 1024 ** 3, days=-1, created=base + timedelta(hours=2))
        rows = rows_in(self.client.get(LIST).content.decode())
        self.assertEqual([(row["cells"]["File"], row["cells"]["Size"], row["cells"]["Secret flags"], row["state"]) for row in rows],
                         [("gone.zip", "3.0 GB", "None", "expired"), ("second.txt", "2.0 KB", "Stripe key", "live"), ("first.txt", "100 B", "None", "live")])

    def test_a_held_file_is_held_and_has_no_controls(self):
        self.make_file("held.txt", held=True)

                         "backend/dashboard/file_rows.py: held_ids marks the files the safety review holds, which the list body does not say")

    def test_only_the_owners_files_are_listed(self):

        self.assertNotIn(theirs.token, html)
        self.assertNotIn(str(theirs.id), html)

    def test_a_workspace_with_no_files_says_so(self):
```
