```python
        self.assertEqual(main.count("autofocus"), 1, f"{MADE_PAGE}: one element takes focus on load")
        self.assertLess(main.index('id="key-warning"'), main.index('id="new-key"'), f"{MADE_PAGE}: the warning comes before the key in the reading order")

    def test_the_page_is_a_form_page_with_its_own_title_and_a_way_back(self):
        html = self.create("shown").content.decode()
        main = main_of(html)
        self.assertIn("<title>New API key | Veilfile</title>", html, f"{MADE_PAGE}: title the page New API key | Veilfile")
        self.assertEqual(re.findall(r"<h1[^>]*>(.*?)</h1>", main), ["Your new API key"], f"{MADE_PAGE}: one h1 inside <main>")
        self.assertRegex(html, r'<body class="[^"]*\blayout-form\b', f"{MADE_PAGE}: extend layouts/form.html: the key is not on a page that changes in place")
        self.assertNotIn("data-layout", html, f"{MADE_PAGE}: no layout family: the answer to a POST loads as an ordinary page")
        self.assertIn('<a class="action interactive" href="/app/keys/">Done</a>', main, f"{MADE_PAGE}: Done goes back to Keys, as the main action")
        self.assertIn("Name: <strong>shown</strong>", main, f"{MADE_PAGE}: say which key this is")

    def test_a_blank_name_is_untitled_key_and_a_name_is_stripped(self):
        self.create("   ")
        self.create("  padded  ")
        self.assertEqual(sorted(APIKey.objects.values_list("name", flat=True)), ["Untitled key", "padded"],
                         f"{KEYS_VIEW}: the name goes through KeyForm and account.create_key: stripped, and Untitled key when blank")

    def test_a_255_character_name_is_accepted_and_shown_whole(self):
        name = "n" * 255
        response = self.create(name)
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200, f"{FORMS}: 255 characters is the longest name the model takes")
        self.assertIn(f"Name: <strong>{name}</strong>", response.content.decode(), f"{MADE_PAGE}: print the name whole")

    def test_a_name_is_escaped_on_the_page_that_shows_the_key(self):
        html = self.create("<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>").content.decode()
        self.assertNotIn("<img src=x", html, f"{MADE_PAGE}: the name is a visitor's words: print it escaped")

    def test_making_a_key_is_recorded_in_the_funnel(self):
        self.create()
        self.assertTrue(FunnelEvent.objects.filter(stage=funnel.KEY_ISSUED, workspace=self.workspace).exists(),
                        "backend/drop_core/account.py: create_key records the key_issued funnel event, as the JSON endpoint does")

    def test_the_funnel_event_keeps_the_browsers_anonymous_id(self):
        self.client.cookies["vf_funnel"] = "a" * 32 + ".l"
        self.create()
        event = FunnelEvent.objects.get(stage=funnel.KEY_ISSUED, workspace=self.workspace)
        self.assertEqual(event.anonymous_id, "a" * 32, f"{KEYS_VIEW}: _create passes request=request to account.create_key, so funnel.record sees the browser's vf_funnel cookie")

    def test_the_next_visit_lists_the_key_by_its_prefix_only(self):
        raw = KEY.findall(self.create("listed").content.decode())[0]
        html = self.keys_page().content.decode()
        row = TableRows(html).rows[0]
        self.assertEqual((row["Name"], row["Prefix"], row["State"]), ("listed", raw[:12], "Active"), f"{KEYS_PAGE}: the new key is listed with its prefix")
        self.assertNotIn(raw, html, f"{KEYS_PAGE}: a later visit never shows the whole key")


class RawKeyIsKeptNowhereTests(SignedInCase):
    """AGENTS.md invariant 1: the raw key exists only in the answer to the POST that made it."""

    def make(self):
        """Make a key with the logs watched; return the answer, the raw key, the logs and the token the POST carried."""
        token = hidden_token(self.keys_page().content.decode())
        with watching_logs() as logs, self.assertNoLogs("dashboard", level="DEBUG"):
            response = self.create("secretive", token=token)
        raw = KEY.findall(response.content.decode())
        self.assertEqual(len(raw), 1, "the POST must show the key once, or these checks prove nothing")
        return response, raw[0], logs, token

    def test_not_in_the_session(self):
        _, raw, _, _ = self.make()
        self.assertNotIn(raw, json.dumps(dict(self.client.session)), f"{KEYS_VIEW}: never put a key in the session (invariant 1)")
        for row in Session.objects.all():
            self.assertNotIn(raw, json.dumps(SessionStore().decode(row.session_data)), f"{KEYS_VIEW}: no stored session holds the key (invariant 1)")

    def test_not_in_a_message(self):
        response, raw, _, _ = self.make()
        self.assertEqual([str(message) for message in get_messages(response.wsgi_request)], [],
                         f"{KEYS_VIEW}: a new key sends no message at all; nothing secret goes into one (invariant 1)")
        later = self.keys_page()
        self.assertNotIn(raw, later.content.decode(), f"{KEYS_VIEW}: no message carries the key to the next page")

    def test_not_in_a_cookie_or_a_header(self):
        response, raw, _, _ = self.make()
        jars = [response.cookies, self.client.cookies]
        for jar in jars:
            for name, morsel in jar.items():
                self.assertNotIn(raw, morsel.value, f"{KEYS_VIEW}: the cookie {name} must not hold the key (invariant 1)")
        for name, value in response.headers.items():
            self.assertNotIn(raw, value, f"{KEYS_VIEW}: the header {name} must not hold the key (invariant 1)")

    def test_not_in_any_log_record(self):
        _, raw, logs, _ = self.make()
        self.assertEqual([line for line in logs.lines if raw in line], [], f"{KEYS_VIEW}: nothing logs the key (invariant 1)")
        self.assertEqual([line for line in logs.lines if raw[4:] in line], [], f"{KEYS_VIEW}: nothing logs the part of the key after vlf_ either")

    def test_not_in_the_cache(self):
        _, raw, _, _ = self.make()
        for name, blob in cache._cache.items():  # the in-process cache tests run with (DEBUG): its values are pickles
            self.assertNotIn(raw.encode(), blob, f"{KEYS_VIEW}: the cache entry {name} must not hold the key (invariant 1)")

    def test_not_in_the_database_beyond_its_hash(self):
        _, raw, _, _ = self.make()
        key = APIKey.objects.get()
        self.assertEqual(key.key_hash, hashlib.sha256(raw.encode()).hexdigest(), "backend/drop_core/models.py: only the SHA-256 hash is stored")
        for field in key._meta.concrete_fields:
            self.assertNotIn(raw, str(getattr(key, field.attname)), f"backend/drop_core/models.py: APIKey.{field.name} must not hold the raw key")

    def test_not_in_the_next_page_or_a_reload(self):
        _, raw, _, token = self.make()
        for url in (KEYS_URL, "/app/", APPS_URL, f"{KEYS_URL}?again=1"):
            self.assertNotIn(raw, self.client.get(url).content.decode(), f"{KEYS_VIEW}: {url} must not show the key after the POST that made it")
        resent = self.client.post(KEYS_URL, {"name": "secretive", "token": token})
        self.assertNotIn(raw, resent.content.decode(), f"{KEYS_VIEW}: a reload (the POST sent again) must not show the key")

    def test_a_failure_after_the_token_is_spent_leaves_it_spent(self):
        """SessionMiddleware saves nothing after a 500. Without the explicit save, a crash once the key exists would let a retry make a second one."""
        client = Client(raise_request_exception=False)
        client.force_login(self.user)
        token = hidden_token(client.get(KEYS_URL).content.decode())
        with mock.patch("dashboard.keys.account.create_key", side_effect=RuntimeError("database went away")), \
                self.assertLogs("django.request", level="ERROR"):
            response = client.post(KEYS_URL, {"name": "x", "token": token})
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 500)
        self.assertNotIn(token, client.session.get(forms.KEY_TOKENS, []), f"{KEYS_VIEW}: _create saves the session once the token is spent (request.session.save())")


class ResentPostTests(SignedInCase):
    """A reload resends the POST. The token it carries is spent, so it makes no second key and says why."""

    def test_the_same_token_twice_makes_one_key(self):
        token = hidden_token(self.keys_page().content.decode())
        first = self.create(token=token)
        second = self.create(token=token)
        self.assertEqual(first.status_code, 200, f"{KEYS_VIEW}: the first POST makes the key")
        self.assertEqual(second.status_code, 409, f"{KEYS_VIEW}: a spent token is a conflict: 409, and never 200, which means a key was made")
        self.assertEqual(APIKey.objects.count(), 1, f"{KEYS_VIEW}: a resent POST makes no second key")
        self.assertEqual(KEY.findall(second.content.decode()), [], f"{KEYS_VIEW}: the second answer shows no key")

    def test_the_answer_says_no_key_was_made_and_why(self):
        token = hidden_token(self.keys_page().content.decode())
        self.create(token=token)
        html = self.create(token=token).content.decode()
        from dashboard import keys  # imported here so that the forms' tests run before keys.py exists
        self.assertIn(unescape(keys.SPENT), unescape(html), f"{KEYS_VIEW}: SPENT is the sentence a spent token gets")
        self.assertIn('<div class="form-errors" role="alert" tabindex="-1" autofocus>', html, f"{KEYS_PAGE}: the sentence is the form_errors alert, and takes focus")
        self.assertEqual(main_of(html).count("autofocus"), 1, f"{KEYS_PAGE}: one element takes focus: the alert")
        self.assertEqual(re.findall(r"<h1[^>]*>(.*?)</h1>", main_of(html)), ["Keys"], f"{KEYS_PAGE}: the answer is the Keys page")
        self.assertEqual(TableRows(html).rows[0]["Name"], "ci-runner", f"{KEYS_PAGE}: the list is there, with the key that was made")
        self.assertIn("no-store", self.create(token=token).get("Cache-Control", ""), f"{KEYS_VIEW}: this page carries a token too")

    def test_the_answer_has_a_fresh_form_that_works(self):
        token = hidden_token(self.keys_page().content.decode())
        self.create(token=token)
        again = self.create(token=token)
        fresh = hidden_token(again.content.decode())
        self.assertNotEqual(fresh, token, f"{KEYS_VIEW}: the page after a refusal carries a new token")
        self.assertEqual(self.create(token=fresh).status_code, 200, f"{KEYS_VIEW}: the new token makes a key")
        self.assertEqual(APIKey.objects.count(), 2)

    def test_a_token_nobody_issued_makes_no_key(self):
        for data in ({"name": "x", "token": "made-up"}, {"name": "x", "token": ""}, {"name": "x"}):
            with self.subTest(data=data):
                self.keys_page()
                response = self.client.post(KEYS_URL, data)
                self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 409, f"{KEYS_VIEW}: a POST without a token this session issued is refused with 409")
        self.assertEqual(APIKey.objects.count(), 0, f"{KEYS_VIEW}: no token, no key")

    def test_another_sessions_token_makes_no_key(self):
        other = Client()
        other.force_login(make_user("someone", plan="team"))
        theirs = hidden_token(other.get(KEYS_URL).content.decode())
        response = self.client.post(KEYS_URL, {"name": "x", "token": theirs})
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 409, f"{FORMS}: a token is good in the session that was issued it only")
        self.assertEqual(APIKey.objects.count(), 0)

    def test_two_tabs_each_make_a_key(self):
        one = hidden_token(self.keys_page().content.decode())
        two = hidden_token(self.keys_page().content.decode())
        self.assertEqual(self.create(token=two).status_code, 200, f"{FORMS}: the second tab's token works")
        self.assertEqual(self.create(token=one).status_code, 200, f"{FORMS}: and the first tab's still works: the session keeps the last {forms.KEPT_TOKENS}")
        self.assertEqual(APIKey.objects.count(), 2)

    def test_the_sixth_page_retires_the_first_form(self):
        first = hidden_token(self.keys_page().content.decode())
        for _ in range(forms.KEPT_TOKENS):
            self.keys_page()
        self.assertEqual(self.create(token=first).status_code, 409, f"{FORMS}: a form six pages old is out of date")
        self.assertEqual(APIKey.objects.count(), 0)

    def test_a_missing_csrf_token_is_the_form_not_sent_page_and_makes_no_key(self):
        client = Client(enforce_csrf_checks=True)
        client.force_login(self.user)
        token = hidden_token(client.get(KEYS_URL).content.decode())
        with self.assertLogs("django.security.csrf", level="WARNING"):
            response = client.post(KEYS_URL, {"name": "x", "token": token})
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 403, "backend/config/settings.py: CSRF_FAILURE_VIEW answers a POST without the CSRF token with 403")
        self.assertIn("Form not sent.", response.content.decode(), "backend/pages/errors.py: the shell's Form not sent page")
        self.assertEqual(APIKey.objects.count(), 0, f"{KEYS_VIEW}: a POST without the CSRF token makes no key")
        self.assertEqual(client.session[forms.KEY_TOKENS], [token], f"{KEYS_VIEW}: and does not spend the token: the form on the page still works")


class RefusalTests(SignedInCase):
    """Each refusal answers the Keys page with the status the JSON endpoint gives it, a sentence of its own and no key. A 200 means a key was made."""

    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        self.keys_before = 0

    def refused(self, response, status):
        """The answer is the Keys page with this status, shows no key and made none (keys_before is how many there were)."""
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, status, f"{KEYS_VIEW}: a refusal has the JSON endpoint's status")
        self.assertEqual(KEY.findall(response.content.decode()), [], f"{KEYS_VIEW}: a refusal shows no key")
        self.assertEqual(APIKey.objects.count(), self.keys_before, f"{KEYS_VIEW}: a refusal makes no key")
        self.assertEqual(re.findall(r"<h1[^>]*>(.*?)</h1>", main_of(response.content.decode())), ["Keys"], f"{KEYS_PAGE}: a refusal answers the Keys page")
        self.assertIn("no-store", response.get("Cache-Control", ""), f"{KEYS_VIEW}: the page after a refusal carries a token, so it is never cached")

    def test_an_unverified_email_is_403_with_a_sentence_and_a_way_to_verify(self):
        EmailVerification.objects.filter(user=self.user).update(is_verified=False)
        response = self.create("waiting")
        html = response.content.decode()
        self.refused(response, 403)
        self.assertIn("Verify your email address before creating API keys. Check your inbox for the verification link.", html,
                      f"{KEYS_VIEW}: say the endpoint's sentence")
        self.assertIn('<a class="label interactive" href="/accounts/verify-email/">Verify your email</a>', html, f"{KEYS_PAGE}: link to /accounts/verify-email/")
        self.assertIn('<div class="form-errors" role="alert" tabindex="-1" autofocus>', html, f"{KEYS_PAGE}: the refusal is the alert and takes focus")
        self.assertIn('value="waiting"', html, f"{KEYS_PAGE}: the name typed is kept")

    def test_the_name_kept_after_a_refusal_is_escaped(self):
        EmailVerification.objects.filter(user=self.user).update(is_verified=False)
        html = self.create('a" autofocus onfocus="alert(1)').content.decode()
        field = next(attrs for attrs in tags(html, "input") if attrs.get("id") == "id_name")
        self.assertEqual(field.get("value"), 'a" autofocus onfocus="alert(1)', f"{KEYS_PAGE}: the field component prints value escaped: the quote stays inside the attribute")
        self.assertNotIn("onfocus", {name for name in field}, f"{KEYS_PAGE}: a name must not become an attribute of the input")

    def test_the_plans_key_cap_is_402_and_names_the_limit(self):
        self.make_key("one")
        self.workspace.plan = "free"
        self.workspace.save()
        self.keys_before = 1
        response = self.create("second")
        html = response.content.decode()
        self.refused(response, 402)
        cap = PLANS["free"]["keys"]
        self.assertIn(f"Your Free plan allows {cap} active key. Revoke one below to make room, or change plans.", html, f"{KEYS_VIEW}: _refusal says the plan's cap, from plans.py")
        self.assertIn('<a class="label interactive" href="/app/billing/">Billing</a>', html, f"{KEYS_PAGE}: link to Billing")

    def test_a_cap_above_one_says_keys(self):
        for index in range(PLANS["team"]["keys"]):
            self.make_key(f"k{index}")
        self.keys_before = PLANS["team"]["keys"]
        response = self.create("one more")
        self.refused(response, 402)
        self.assertIn(f"Your Team plan allows {PLANS['team']['keys']} active keys.", response.content.decode(), f"{KEYS_VIEW}: plural for more than one")

    def test_a_workspace_over_its_cap_after_a_downgrade_is_still_refused(self):
        for index in range(3):
            self.make_key(f"k{index}")
        self.workspace.plan = "free"
        self.workspace.save()
        self.keys_before = 3
        self.refused(self.create("more"), 402)

    def test_a_revoked_key_makes_room(self):
        self.workspace.plan = "free"
        self.workspace.save()
        self.make_key("old", active=False)
        self.assertEqual(self.create("fresh").status_code, 200, "backend/drop_core/key_caps.py: only active keys count toward the cap")

    def test_a_name_that_is_too_long_is_a_field_error(self):
        response = self.create("x" * 256)
        html = response.content.decode()
        self.refused(response, 400)
        field = next(attrs for attrs in tags(html, "input") if attrs.get("id") == "id_name")
        self.assertEqual(field.get("aria-invalid"), "true", f"{KEYS_PAGE}: the name field is marked invalid")
        self.assertIn("id_name_error", field.get("aria-describedby", ""), f"{KEYS_PAGE}: and tied to its error")
        self.assertIn('<div class="field__error" id="id_name_error">', html, f"{KEYS_PAGE}: the error is the field component's")
        self.assertIn("<p>Use 255 characters or fewer.</p>", html, f"{FORMS}: say the limit")
        self.assertIn("autofocus", field, f"{KEYS_PAGE}: focus goes to the field in error (focus_field)")
        self.assertEqual(main_of(html).count("autofocus"), 1, f"{KEYS_PAGE}: one element takes focus")
        self.assertNotIn('role="alert"', main_of(html), f"{KEYS_PAGE}: an error of the field is not also a summary")
        self.assertIn('value="' + "x" * 256 + '"', html, f"{KEYS_PAGE}: the name typed is kept")

    def test_a_name_with_a_line_break_is_a_field_error(self):
        response = self.create("two\nlines")
        self.refused(response, 400)
        self.assertIn("<p>Use a single line of plain text.</p>", response.content.decode(), f"{FORMS}: say what to do")

    def test_a_refusal_has_a_form_that_works(self):
        EmailVerification.objects.filter(user=self.user).update(is_verified=False)
        html = self.create("first").content.decode()
        EmailVerification.objects.filter(user=self.user).update(is_verified=True)
        response = self.client.post(KEYS_URL, {"name": "second", "token": hidden_token(html)})
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200, f"{KEYS_VIEW}: the page after a refusal carries a new token, so the person can send it again")

    def test_only_a_key_made_answers_200(self):
        self.workspace.plan = "free"
        self.workspace.save()
        statuses = [self.create("a").status_code, self.create("b").status_code, self.create("c" * 256).status_code]
        self.assertEqual(statuses, [200, 402, 400], f"{KEYS_VIEW}: 200 is the key being made; a refusal never answers 200")

    def test_an_answer_this_page_does_not_know_is_shown_with_its_own_message(self):
        unknown = account.Answer(429, {"error": "Slow down.", "code": "rate_limited"})
        with mock.patch("dashboard.keys.account.create_key", return_value=unknown):
            response = self.create("x")
        self.refused(response, 429)
        self.assertIn("Slow down.", response.content.decode(), f"{KEYS_VIEW}: _refusal falls back to the endpoint's message and status: never a 500, never a blank page")


class RevokeKeyTests(SignedInCase):
    def url(self, key):
        return f"{KEYS_URL}{key.id}/revoke/"

    def test_the_confirmation_page_asks_and_changes_nothing(self):
        key, raw = self.make_key("deploy")
        response = self.client.get(self.url(key))
        html = response.content.decode()
        main = main_of(html)
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(re.findall(r"<h1[^>]*>(.*?)</h1>", main), ["Revoke this API key?"], f"{REVOKE_PAGE}: the React dashboard's question is the heading")
        self.assertIn("<p>Agents using it will fail.</p>", main, f"{REVOKE_PAGE}: and its warning")
        self.assertIn("<dd>deploy</dd>", main, f"{REVOKE_PAGE}: name the key")
        self.assertIn(f"<dd><code>{key.key_prefix}</code></dd>", main, f"{REVOKE_PAGE}: and its prefix")
        self.assertIn("<title>Revoke key | Veilfile</title>", html, f"{REVOKE_PAGE}: title the page Revoke key | Veilfile")
        self.assertEqual(response.get("X-Robots-Tag"), NOINDEX, f"{KEYS_VIEW}: dashboard_view adds the noindex header")
        self.assertIn('<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">', html, f"{REVOKE_PAGE}: the robots meta")
        self.assertEqual(len(re.findall('name="csrfmiddlewaretoken"', main)), 1, f"{REVOKE_PAGE}: the form holds the CSRF token")
        self.assertIn('<button class="action interactive" type="submit">Revoke key</button>', main, f"{REVOKE_PAGE}: the main action")
        self.assertIn('<a class="label interactive" href="/app/keys/">Keep this key</a>', main, f"{REVOKE_PAGE}: the quiet way out")
        key.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertTrue(key.is_active, f"{KEYS_VIEW}: a GET never revokes")
        self.assertEqual(APIKey.verify(raw), key, f"{KEYS_VIEW}: the key still works after a GET")

    def test_it_is_a_form_page_like_the_others(self):
        key, _ = self.make_key("deploy")
        form_pages.FormPagesAreOnTheShellTests.check(self, self.url(key))

    def test_the_post_revokes_and_goes_back_with_one_line(self):
        key, raw = self.make_key("deploy")
        response = self.client.post(self.url(key))
        self.assertEqual((response.status_code, response.get("Location")), (302, KEYS_URL), f"{KEYS_VIEW}: a revoke redirects to Keys")
        key.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertFalse(key.is_active, f"{KEYS_VIEW}: the POST revokes the key")
        self.assertIsNone(APIKey.verify(raw), "the revoked key authenticates no more")
        html = self.client.get(KEYS_URL).content.decode()
        self.assertEqual(Notices(html).found, ["Key revoked."], "backend/templates/layouts/app.html: a message is a .notice with role=status at the top of <main>")
        row = TableRows(html).rows[0]
        self.assertEqual((row["State"], row["links"]), ("Revoked", []), f"{KEYS_PAGE}: the key stays listed, as Revoked")

    def test_the_line_is_shown_once(self):
        key, _ = self.make_key("deploy")
        self.client.post(self.url(key))
        self.client.get(KEYS_URL)
        self.assertNotIn("Key revoked.", self.client.get(KEYS_URL).content.decode(), f"{KEYS_VIEW}: a message is read once; a reload does not repeat it")

    def test_another_workspaces_key_is_a_404_and_stays_active(self):
        theirs, raw = APIKey.create_key(get_or_create_workspace(make_user("other", plan="team")), "theirs")
        for method in (self.client.get, self.client.post):
            response = method(self.url(theirs))
            self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 404, f"{KEYS_VIEW}: key_revoke looks the key up in the signed-in person's workspace: another's is the shell's 404")
            self.assertIn("Not found.", response.content.decode(), "backend/templates/404.html: the shell's 404 page")
            self.assertEqual(response.get("X-Robots-Tag"), NOINDEX, f"{KEYS_VIEW}: return the 404 (do not raise it) so dashboard_view adds the noindex header")
        theirs.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertTrue(theirs.is_active)
        self.assertEqual(APIKey.verify(raw), theirs)

    def test_a_missing_or_malformed_id_is_a_404_never_a_500(self):
        for path in (f"{KEYS_URL}999999/revoke/", f"{KEYS_URL}{10**30}/revoke/", f"{KEYS_URL}abc/revoke/", f"{KEYS_URL}-1/revoke/", f"{KEYS_URL}1.5/revoke/"):
            for method in (self.client.get, self.client.post):
                with self.subTest(path=path, method=method.__name__):
                    self.assertEqual(method(path).status_code, 404, f"backend/dashboard/urls.py: {path} is the shell's 404")

    def test_a_key_already_revoked_says_so_and_changes_nothing(self):
        key, _ = self.make_key("old", active=False)
        for method in (self.client.get, self.client.post):
            response = method(self.url(key))
            self.assertEqual((response.status_code, response.get("Location")), (302, KEYS_URL), f"{KEYS_VIEW}: key_revoke sends a revoked key back to Keys")
```

- [ ] **Step 4: The form and the token**

Create `backend/dashboard/forms.py`:

```python
"""Forms of the dashboard: the new-key form and the one-time token that keeps a resent POST from making a second key."""
import secrets
import unicodedata

from django import forms

from drop_core.models import APIKey

# The unspent form tokens of the Keys page, newest last, in request.session. A token is not a secret (it only says "this form has not been
# sent yet"), but it must be one the page really issued, so a POST made up by hand, or sent twice, makes no key.
KEY_TOKENS = "dashboard_key_tokens"
KEPT_TOKENS = 5  # the last few, so a second tab's form still works; a sixth page in a row retires the oldest
NAME_LENGTH = APIKey._meta.get_field("name").max_length


def issue_key_token(session):
    """A new token for a Keys page, remembered in the session with the last KEPT_TOKENS - 1 unspent ones."""
    held = session.get(KEY_TOKENS)
    kept = [other for other in held if isinstance(other, str)] if isinstance(held, list) else []
    token = secrets.token_urlsafe(16)
    session[KEY_TOKENS] = [*kept[-(KEPT_TOKENS - 1):], token]
    return token


def spend_key_token(session, token):
    """True once for an unspent token the session holds; the token is gone from the session before this returns. Anything else (a spent token,
    one of another session, none at all) is False."""
    held = session.get(KEY_TOKENS)
    if not isinstance(token, str) or not token or not isinstance(held, list) or token not in held:
        return False
    session[KEY_TOKENS] = [other for other in held if other != token]
    return True


class KeyForm(forms.Form):
    """The new key's name: optional (the key is then "Untitled key"), one line, at most as long as the model allows. The same rules as the
    JSON endpoint's, said as sentences for a person."""

    name = forms.CharField(
        required=False,
        strip=True,
        max_length=NAME_LENGTH,
        error_messages={
            "max_length": f"Use {NAME_LENGTH} characters or fewer.",
            "null_characters_not_allowed": "Use a single line of plain text.",
        },
    )

    def clean_name(self):
        name = self.cleaned_data["name"]
        if any(unicodedata.category(char) == "Cc" for char in name):
            raise forms.ValidationError("Use a single line of plain text.")
        return name
```

Create `backend/dashboard/keys.py`:

```python
"""Keys and Connected apps (spec 4.8): the pages that show a person's credentials and take them back.

Invariant 1 (AGENTS.md): a new key's raw value lives in one place only, the answer to the POST that made it. It is never put in the session, a
message, a cookie, a URL, a log or the cache, and that answer is `Cache-Control: no-store`. The POST also carries a one-time token (forms.py)
that the Keys page issued, so a reload, which resends the POST, finds it spent and makes no second key.

A 200 from the Keys POST therefore always means a key was made and is on the page; every refusal has the status the JSON endpoint gives it
(400, 402, 403) or 409 for a spent token.
"""
from datetime import datetime

from django.contrib import messages
from django.shortcuts import redirect, render
from django.views.decorators.http import require_http_methods

from drop_core import account
from drop_core.key_caps import key_cap
from drop_core.models import APIKey, get_or_create_workspace
from pages.errors import not_found

from .forms import KeyForm, issue_key_token, spend_key_token
from .views import dashboard_view

SPENT = (
    "That form was already used or is out of date, so no key was made. A key is shown only once, when it is made. "
    "If you didn't copy yours, revoke it below and make a new one."
)
ALREADY_REVOKED = "That key was already revoked."


def _when(value):
    """An ISO time string of an account function's answer as an aware datetime, or None."""
    return datetime.fromisoformat(value) if value else None


def _key_rows(user):
    return [
        {**item, "created_at": _when(item["created_at"]), "last_used_at": _when(item["last_used_at"])}
        for item in account.list_keys(user).body
    ]


def _keys_page(request, form, status=200, refusal=None):
    """The Keys page with a fresh form token. A page that is the answer to a refused POST has the refusal's status and says why; none of them
    holds a key."""
    context = {"rows": _key_rows(request.user), "form": form, "token": issue_key_token(request.session), "refusal": refusal}
    response = render(request, "dashboard/keys.html", context, status=status)
    response["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"  # the form carries a one-time token, and Back must not show a spent one
    return response


def _refusal(user, answer):
    """The kind of a refused create_key and the sentence for it. The codes are the JSON endpoint's; one this page does not know shows the
    endpoint's own message."""
    body = answer.body if isinstance(answer.body, dict) else {}
    message = body.get("error") or "No key was made."
    code = body.get("code")
    if code == "email_verification_required":
        return {"kind": "unverified", "message": message}
    if code == "key_limit_reached":
        workspace = get_or_create_workspace(user)
        cap = key_cap(workspace)
        if cap is not None:
            message = (
                f"Your {workspace.plan.capitalize()} plan allows {cap} active {'key' if cap == 1 else 'keys'}. "
                "Revoke one below to make room, or change plans."
            )
        return {"kind": "cap", "message": message}
    return {"kind": "other", "message": message}


def _key_made(request, answer):
    """The one page that shows a key: the answer to the POST that made it, 200, never cached."""
    body = answer.body
    raw_key = body["api_key"]
    # shell_page is emptied, as pages/errors.py does: the answer is at the Keys address, whose section entry would make it a page that changes in place.
    context = {"shell_page": None, "key_name": body["name"], "new_key": raw_key}
    response = render(request, "dashboard/key_made.html", context)
    response["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"
    return response


def _create(request):
    if not spend_key_token(request.session, request.POST.get("token")):
        return _keys_page(request, KeyForm(), 409, {"kind": "spent", "message": SPENT})
    # Spent before the key is made, and saved now: SessionMiddleware saves nothing after a 500, so a failure once the key exists would
    # otherwise leave the token spendable, and a retry would make a second key.
    request.session.save()
    form = KeyForm(request.POST)
    if not form.is_valid():
        return _keys_page(request, form, 400)
    answer = account.create_key(request.user, form.cleaned_data["name"], request=request)
    if answer.status == 201:
        return _key_made(request, answer)
    return _keys_page(request, form, answer.status, _refusal(request.user, answer))


@dashboard_view
@require_http_methods(["GET", "HEAD", "POST"])
def keys(request):
    if request.method == "POST":
        return _create(request)
    return _keys_page(request, KeyForm())


def _own_key(user, key_id):
    """The key of this person's workspace with this id, or None: another workspace's key and a missing one are the same."""
    return APIKey.objects.filter(pk=key_id, workspace=get_or_create_workspace(user)).first()


@dashboard_view
@require_http_methods(["GET", "HEAD", "POST"])
def key_revoke(request, key_id):
    key = _own_key(request.user, key_id)
    if key is None:
        return not_found(request)
    if not key.is_active:
        messages.info(request, ALREADY_REVOKED)
        return redirect("app-keys")
    if request.method == "POST":
        if account.revoke_key(request.user, key.pk).status != 204:
            return not_found(request)
        messages.success(request, "Key revoked.")
        return redirect("app-keys")
    return render(request, "dashboard/key_revoke.html", {"key": key})


def _app_rows(user):
    return [{**item, "last_authorized_at": _when(item["last_authorized_at"])} for item in account.list_grants(user).body]


@dashboard_view
@require_http_methods(["GET", "HEAD"])
def apps(request):
    return render(request, "dashboard/apps.html", {"rows": _app_rows(request.user)})


@dashboard_view
@require_http_methods(["GET", "HEAD", "POST"])
def app_disconnect(request, app_id):
    app = next((row for row in _app_rows(request.user) if row["id"] == app_id), None)
    if app is None:
        return not_found(request)
    if request.method == "POST":
        if account.disconnect_grant(request.user, app_id).status != 204:
            return not_found(request)
        messages.success(request, f"{app['name']} disconnected.")
        return redirect("app-apps")
    return render(request, "dashboard/app_disconnect.html", {"app": app})
```

### Task 6: Billing

The Billing section (`/app/billing/`) becomes ordinary pages, using the billing functions Task 1 extracted. It keeps what the React `BillingSection` did and every sentence it said, except the sentences for a refusal, which are now fixed sentences in the customer's words:

- the plan and Stripe's status for it, the four status warnings and the over-limit lines (Task 3's include);
- "Upgrade to {Plan} ($N/mo)" for a workspace with no subscription, a POST to checkout that sends the browser to Stripe;
- "Switch to {Plan} ($N/mo)" for a subscriber, a link to a confirmation page that carries the `switchConfirmText` sentences and whose POST switches;
- "Manage billing", a POST that sends the browser to the Stripe portal;
- an unpaid switch (`payment_required`) with "Complete payment" and "Keep {Plan}";
- one fixed sentence for every refusal. Stripe's own text, the API's codes and the word "instance" never reach the page; a failure that the page cannot explain ends with "Reference: XXXXXX", and one `billing: dashboard refusal ref=XXXXXX` log line holds what Stripe said.

Nothing on these pages changes anything on a GET, and no GET creates a Stripe session. Each failure is one sentence on the Billing page after a redirect, never a 500.

**Files:**
- Create: `backend/dashboard/billing_page.py`, `backend/dashboard/tests_billing.py`
- Create (template): `backend/templates/dashboard/billing_switch.html`
- Modify: `backend/dashboard/views.py` (the billing stub Task 2 left becomes the real views, and the imports they need), `backend/dashboard/urls.py` (three routes), `backend/pages/registry.py` (three entries in `DASHBOARD_SECTIONS`)
- Modify (template): `backend/templates/dashboard/billing.html` (replaces Task 2's stub)
- Modify (tests): `backend/drop_core/tests_fix_docs.py` (the pricing scan reads `billing_page.py`), `backend/pages/tests_site_rules.py` (`READING_TEST_MODULES`)
- Modify (docs): `AGENTS.md` ("Pricing changes"), `docs/stripe-live-launch-runbook.md` (the two places that say the dashboard shows the Stripe error)
- Never touch: `backend/legal/documents/*`, `backend/drop_billing/*` (Task 1's functions are used as they are), `backend/templates/dashboard/over_limits.html` (Task 3 makes it; Billing only includes it), `docs/API.md`, `docs/llms.txt`

No new package directory is made: `backend/dashboard/__init__.py` is Task 2's.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes (Task 1):
  - `drop_billing.account.status(user)`, `checkout(user, plan)`, `switch(user, plan)` and `portal(user)`. Each returns `drop_core.account.Answer(status, body, headers)`. The `body` is exactly what the JSON endpoint answers:
    - `status` gives 200 and `plan`, `caps`, `storage_used_bytes`, `active_keys`, `over_plan_limits`, `has_billing_account`, `has_subscription`, `subscription_status`;
    - `checkout` gives 200 `{"checkout_url"}`, 400 `{"error": "invalid_plan"}`, 409 `already_subscribed`, 502 `stripe_error`, 503 `{"error": "billing_not_configured"}`;
    - `switch` gives 200 `{"plan", "status"}` with `status` one of `switched`, `unchanged`, `pending_cancelled`, or 402 `payment_required` (with `invoice_url`), 409 (`subscription_past_due`, `no_subscription`, `multiple_subscriptions`), 502 and 503;
    - `ALREADY_SUBSCRIBED_MESSAGES` (wherever Task 1 leaves it; its draft has it in `drop_billing/account.py`): the advice for a checkout that a live subscription blocks, by that subscription's status (`active` and `trialing`, `past_due`, `unpaid`, `incomplete`, `paused`). The 409 body carries `subscription_status`.
    - `portal` gives 200 `{"portal_url"}`, 400 `{"error": "no_billing_account"}`, 502, 503.
  - Nothing in this task calls Stripe except through them. The tests patch the Stripe library, so they do not depend on which module Task 1 put the code in.

  - `dashboard/billing.html` (on `layouts/app.html`) and `dashboard/billing_switch.html` (on `layouts/form.html`: an ordinary page load, no `data-layout`). Billing includes Task 3's `dashboard/over_limits.html` as `{% include "dashboard/over_limits.html" with status=status only %}`; this task does not create or change it.
  - `dashboard.billing_page`, whose functions Task 3 may reuse and whose names are fixed here: `paid_plans()`, `plan_name(slug)`, `https_only(url)`, `plan_options(current)`, `is_upgrade(current, target)`, `switch_context(current, target)`, `page_context(status, pending)`, `switch_result(plan, outcome)`, `already_subscribed_sentence(subscription_status)`, `reference()`, `refusal(answer, bad_request, where)`, `body_of(answer)`, `remember_pending(session, plan, invoice_url, now=None)`, `forget_pending(session)`, `pending_for(session, current_plan, now=None)`, with the constants `PENDING_KEY`, `PENDING_SECONDS`, `NOT_CONFIGURED`, `STRIPE_FAILED`, `PAYMENT_FAILED`, `PAST_DUE`, `MULTIPLE_SUBSCRIPTIONS`, `NO_SUCH_PLAN`, `NO_BILLING_ACCOUNT`, `NOT_SUBSCRIBED`, and the table `FIXED`.
  - The session key `dashboard_pending_switch`: `{"plan", "invoice_url", "at"}`, written by a switch answered `payment_required`.
  - One log line per refusal through `logging.getLogger("drop_billing")`: `billing: dashboard refusal ref=<REF> where=<checkout|portal|switch> status=<status> code=<code> message=<Stripe's message>`. The reference is `secrets.token_hex(3).upper()`. The line is ERROR for a failure the page cannot explain (a 502, a 503, an unknown status or code, an address it must not follow) and WARNING for a refusal it explains.
  - The customer sentences, which Task 8's browser checks quote exactly: "Billing isn't available right now. Try again later. Reference: XXXXXX" (a 503: Stripe not connected, as in CI), "Billing couldn't complete that just now. Try again in a moment. Reference: XXXXXX" (a 502, an unknown answer or an address that is not https), the advice for a blocked checkout (drop_billing's `ALREADY_SUBSCRIBED_MESSAGES`, "from this page"), and the fixed sentences in `billing_page.py` (Step 3). `XXXXXX` is six capitals or digits.
  - The pricing scan reads `backend/dashboard/billing_page.py`, and AGENTS.md "Pricing changes" names it.

Background for an engineer new to the repo, and the decisions this task makes:

- **The page, as the React dashboard drew it.** In order: the plan line, one status warning, the pending switch, the over-limit lines, the buttons, and the explanation. Every sentence is the React one (`frontend/src/Dashboard.jsx`, `BillingSection`, `OverLimits`, `switchConfirmText`) except the sentences for a refusal, and the tests pin each. Two things differ from React's page:
  - "Current plan: Team (Stripe status: active)" replaces the badge `team · active`: the middle dot is a non-ASCII character, and the plan is named the way the Plans chapter names it.
  - "Switch to Scale" is a link to a page, where React ran `window.confirm`.

  One thing is kept that looks like a slip: the over-limit heading prints the plan's id as the API gives it ("over the free plan's limits"), as React did.
- **Prices and figures are never typed.** The buttons, the confirmation page's heading and both of its sentences take the price from `PLANS` through `billing_page`. The upgrade sentence is used when the target costs more than the current plan, which is a comparison of prices. A test changes the prices in `PLANS` and watches the pages follow, and another scans these files for a typed `$N` or a typed cap.
- **A failure is a message and a redirect, and the message is in the customer's words.** A POST that Stripe or the setup refuses adds one line with `django.contrib.messages` and redirects to Billing, where Task 2's layout shows it. `billing_page.refusal(answer, bad_request, where)` chooses the line and writes the log line. The owner's rule (2026-10-22) is that the customer never reads Stripe's own text ("Stripe: ..."), a raw code, or operator wording such as "this Veilfile instance" or "until Stripe is connected". So:
  - **Each refusal the page can explain is one fixed sentence, no matter what the API's sentence said.** A 402 `payment_required` is `PAYMENT_FAILED`. A 409 is one of `PAST_DUE`, `NOT_SUBSCRIBED` or `MULTIPLE_SUBSCRIPTIONS` by its `code` (`subscription_past_due`, `no_subscription`, `multiple_subscriptions`). A 409 `already_subscribed` shows the advice for the blocking subscription's status, taken from drop_billing's `ALREADY_SUBSCRIBED_MESSAGES` (Veilfile's own customer copy: reused through Task 1's module, not copied, and not Stripe's text) with "from the dashboard" said as "from this page" by `already_subscribed_sentence`; the response's own `error` text is not used, and no reference is needed. A 400 is a bare code (`invalid_plan`, `no_billing_account`), which the caller says in words. These log at WARNING.
  - **A failure the page cannot explain ends with a reference.** A 502 `stripe_error` and any status or code the page has not seen (and a 200 whose address is not `https://`) is `STRIPE_FAILED` plus " Reference: 4F9A2C". A 503 `billing_not_configured` is `NOT_CONFIGURED` ("Billing isn't available right now. Try again later.") plus the reference. The reference is `secrets.token_hex(3).upper()`: six capitals or digits that a customer can read out. These log at ERROR.
  - **The log line holds the detail.** `billing: dashboard refusal ref=4F9A2C where=checkout status=502 code=stripe_error message='Stripe: Invalid line_items[0]: ...'` goes through `logging.getLogger("drop_billing")` (the logger of `drop_billing/views.py`'s `billing:` lines, which settings routes to the console), so the owner finds Stripe's message by the reference on the page. Stripe's message is cut to 280 characters by the API and written with `%r`, so a newline in it cannot forge a second log line.
  - **The JSON endpoints keep their bodies** (invariant 4): their 502 still reads "Stripe: ..." and their 503 still reads `billing_not_configured`; only the dashboard's page changes.
  - **The runbook follows.** `docs/stripe-live-launch-runbook.md` told the owner to read the Stripe error on the dashboard ("If something breaks", and the Managed Payments note in Phase 4). Step 10 changes both to: the dashboard shows a sentence with a reference, and the `billing:` log line with that reference holds Stripe's message.
- **"Not available" is shown when something was tried, not on a GET.** A GET makes no Stripe call (the status reads the database only), so the page cannot know. React also learned it from a 503. The sentence now arrives as the line after the redirect. The Upgrade buttons stay, and a second try says it again.
- **Manage billing is shown when the workspace has a billing account** (`has_billing_account`: a Stripe customer id is stored). React showed it to everyone until the portal answered `no_billing_account`. A portal POST that finds no account (or Stripe cannot find the customer, which the billing code heals by clearing the id) says so, and the next GET has no button.
- **The unpaid switch is a session hint, with a life of one day.**
  - Why a session: `StatusView` has no field that says a switch is waiting, so nothing a later page load can read says so. React held it in component state, which a reload lost; the session survives that.
  - Written by: a switch POST answered 402 `payment_required`. It stores the plan the visitor asked for (the 402 body's `plan` is the current plan), Stripe's invoice page if it starts with `https://` (else `None`), and the time.
  - Cleared by:
    - any switch answered 200 (switched, unchanged or cancelled), which settles it;
    - the next Billing page, when the entry no longer holds: the workspace is not on a paid plan (the subscription lapsed), is already on the plan the switch named (the invoice was paid and the webhook applied it), the plan is not one that is sold, the entry is not what the code writes, or it is a day old (the page says "Unpaid switches lapse within a day", and so does Stripe).
  - Kept by: a refusal (409, 502, 503). Clearing it there would take away "Keep {Plan}" exactly when the visitor needs to try again.
  - It is not a secret, so Invariant 1 does not apply: a plan, an https invoice page and a time.
- **Checkout and the portal send the browser only where Stripe said.** A 200 answer's address is followed (303) only if it starts with `https://`; anything else (even from a 200) is `STRIPE_FAILED` with a reference, and the address is not printed. The invoice page of a pending switch is held to the same rule where it is stored and again where it is shown.
- **The two POST-only addresses answer a GET with a redirect to Billing**, not a bare 405, because a signed-out visitor who followed a POST address through sign in arrives by GET.
- **The switch confirmation page.**
  - An unknown plan (anything that is not for sale: `free`, `enterprise`, `Team`) is the shell's 404, as a missing object is elsewhere in the dashboard. It is drawn by `pages.errors.not_found` and returned, not raised, so that `dashboard_view` puts the `X-Robots-Tag` header on it as on every `/app/` response.
  - A workspace with no subscription, or one already on that plan, is sent back to Billing with a sentence. There is nothing to confirm: the POST would answer 409 `no_subscription` or `unchanged`.
  - A POST for an unknown plan is the same 404 and changes nothing. A POST for the current plan is allowed: it is how "Keep {Plan}" voids a pending invoice.
  - Checkout's `plan` is a form field, not an address, so an unknown plan there is a sentence on Billing (`NO_SUCH_PLAN`), the way an unknown plan reaches the API as a 400.
  - Its route is in `DASHBOARD_SECTIONS`, marking Billing, as Task 4's `app-file-revoke` marks Files: the confirmation page draws the dashboard's menu with Billing marked and the Sign out button.
- **Tests patch the Stripe library, not `drop_billing.views.stripe`.** The base class `drop_billing.tests_fix_billing.FixBillingBase` patches `Subscription.list`, `Subscription.modify`, `Customer.create`, the checkout and portal `Session.create` and `Invoice.void_invoice`, and points `stripe.api_base` at a closed port, so these tests do not care which module holds the Stripe code and a call a test forgot to patch fails at once. The runner removes `STRIPE_*` from the environment, and the base class puts the test values back. A refusal logs, so each test that causes one runs inside `assertLogs("drop_billing")` (the `refused` helper), which also keeps the line off the test output.
- **The pricing scan.** `backend/templates/**/*.html` is already scanned, so the new templates are. The scan also gets `backend/dashboard/billing_page.py`, the one module that deals in plan figures. The glob does not take `backend/dashboard/*.py`: the scan reads any line that has a plan name next to a number and a unit, which the dashboard's test files may write (a test about 3 keys on the Free plan), and it would fail them for a sentence about a fixture.
- **Not done here, on purpose.**
  - Upgrade, Keep and Manage billing have no confirmation page: React had none, and none of them takes anything away. Only the switch between paid plans asks first (spec 4.8).
  - No new Stripe call, so no new key permission (AGENTS.md: "New Stripe calls in code may need new key permissions"): everything goes through Task 1's functions.
  - The portal returns the visitor to Overview (`return_url` is `/app/`, pinned by `BillingApiTests` and by the JSON contract), not to Billing.
  - A double click on a button sends two requests, as any form does. The second finds the first's result (a second checkout session is harmless; a second switch answers `unchanged`). Each refusal of a double click logs its own reference.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**

**Create `backend/dashboard/tests_billing.py`:**

```python
"""Billing in the dashboard (spec 4.8): the page at /app/billing/, the plan switch and its confirmation page, checkout and the portal.

Stripe is never reached. These tests patch the Stripe library the way drop_billing.tests_fix_billing does, and its base class points
the library's API address at a closed port, so a call that a test forgot to patch fails at once. They pin what a visitor reads:
the React dashboard's sentences, kept; one fixed sentence in the customer's words on the Billing page for every way Stripe or the
setup can refuse, never a 500, and never Stripe's own text, a code or the word "instance" (those, and a reference that finds them, go to
the log); and that only a POST changes anything.

Every class sets longMessage = False, so that a failure prints its own message, which names the file and the fix, and not the
page it searched.
"""
import logging
import os

from datetime import timedelta
from html import unescape

import stripe

TEMPLATES = Path(settings.BASE_DIR) / "templates"
# dashboard/over_limits.html is Task 3's (Overview makes it, Billing includes it); its own tests hold its words.
OWN_TEMPLATES = ("dashboard/billing.html", "dashboard/billing_switch.html")
PAGE = "backend/templates/dashboard/billing.html"
SWITCH_PAGE = "backend/templates/dashboard/billing_switch.html"
VIEWS = "backend/dashboard/views.py"
INVOICE = "https://invoice.stripe.com/i/acct_1/in_pending"
STRIPE_URL = "https://checkout.stripe.com/c/pay/cs_test_1"
PORTAL_URL = "https://billing.stripe.com/p/session/test_1"

# What a visitor reads when Billing refuses. The first two end with "Reference: " and six capitals or digits (REFERENCE below).
NOT_CONFIGURED = "Billing isn't available right now. Try again later."
FAILED = "Billing couldn't complete that just now. Try again in a moment."
PAYMENT_FAILED = "The payment for the plan change did not go through, so your plan is unchanged."
# A checkout that a live subscription blocks gets the advice that fits its status: drop_billing's own customer copy (ALREADY_SUBSCRIBED_MESSAGES,
# reused, not copied), with "from the dashboard" said as "from this page". One phrase of each, so that a wrong pick is seen.
ADVICE = {
    "active": "Switch plans from this page instead of starting a new checkout.",
    "trialing": "Switch plans from this page instead of starting a new checkout.",
    "past_due": "failed payment that Stripe is retrying",
    "unpaid": "has an unpaid invoice",
    "incomplete": "still waiting for its first payment",
    "paused": "subscription is paused",
}
PAST_DUE = "Your last payment failed. Update your payment method under Manage billing before changing plans."
MULTIPLE_SUBSCRIPTIONS = "This workspace has more than one subscription. Use Manage billing to cancel the extra one, or contact support."
NO_SUCH_PLAN = "Choose one of the plans on this page."
NO_BILLING_ACCOUNT = "There is no billing account to manage yet. Upgrade to a paid plan to start one."
NOT_SUBSCRIBED = "You have no subscription to switch yet. Upgrade to a paid plan to start one."
REFERENCE = re.compile(r"Reference: ([0-9A-F]{6})$")
LOGGED = re.compile(r"^billing: dashboard refusal ref=([0-9A-F]{6}) ")
# Words of the operator, which no visitor reads on the page: Stripe's text ("Stripe: ..."), the API's codes, "instance".
OPERATOR_WORDS = ("Stripe:", "instance", "billing_not_configured", "stripe_error", "invalid_plan", "no_billing_account",
                  "payment_required", "already_subscribed", "until Stripe is connected")
# The React dashboard's sentences (frontend/src/Dashboard.jsx), word for word.
WARNINGS = {
    "past_due": "Your last payment failed. Stripe is retrying; update your payment method under Manage billing to keep your plan.",
    "unpaid": ("Your subscription has an unpaid invoice, so this workspace is on the free plan. Pay it, or cancel the "
               "subscription, under Manage billing."),
    "incomplete": ("Your subscription's first payment hasn't gone through. Complete it under Manage billing; an unfinished "
                   "payment expires within a day."),
    "paused": "Your subscription is paused, so this workspace is on the free plan. Resume or cancel it under Manage billing.",
}
EXPLAIN_SUBSCRIBED = ("Plan switches apply to your existing subscription with prorated charges or credits. Manage billing opens "
                      "the Stripe portal for your payment method, invoices, and cancellation.")

                "cancellation in the customer portal.")

                        "confirm), or keep your current plan. Unpaid switches lapse within a day.")

                           "under Manage billing and switch again. Unpaid switches lapse within a day.")


def price(slug):
    return PLANS[slug]["price_usd"]


def name(slug):
    return slug.title()


def main_of(html):
    return html[html.index("<main"):html.index("</main>")]


def attributes(tag):
    return dict(re.findall(r'([\w-]+)="([^"]*)"', tag))


def words(html):
    return " ".join(unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", html)).split())


def forms_in(html):
    """Each <form> in <main>: its attributes, its inputs' attributes and the text of its buttons."""
    return [{
        "attrs": attributes(opening),
        "inputs": [attributes(tag) for tag in re.findall(r"<input\b([^>]*)>", body)],
        "buttons": [words(text) for text in re.findall(r"<button\b[^>]*>(.*?)</button>", body, re.S)],
    } for opening, body in re.findall(r"<form\b([^>]*)>(.*?)</form>", main_of(html), re.S)]


def links_in(html):
    """Each <a> in <main> as (attributes, text)."""
    return [(attributes(opening), words(text)) for opening, text in re.findall(r"<a\b([^>]*)>(.*?)</a>", main_of(html), re.S)]


def value_of(form, input_name):
    return next((tag.get("value") for tag in form["inputs"] if tag.get("name") == input_name), None)


class BillingCase(FixBillingBase):
    """A signed-in workspace with the Stripe library patched. self.ws is the workspace; set_billing, patch_stripe and reload
    are FixBillingBase's."""
    longMessage = False

    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        self.client.force_login(self.user)
        self.billing = reverse("app-billing")
        self.checkout = reverse("app-billing-checkout")
        self.portal = reverse("app-billing-portal")

    def switch_url(self, plan):
        return reverse("app-billing-switch", args=[plan])

    def page(self, url=None):
        """The text of <main> on a page, the way a visitor reads it."""
        response = self.client.get(url or self.billing)
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200, f"{url or self.billing} answered {response.status_code}, not 200")
        return visible_text(response.content.decode())

    def said(self, response):
        """The lines the request left for the next page. Reading them forgets them, so that a test which sends several requests
        (a subTest for each plan) reads only the line of the one it just sent."""
        lines = [str(message) for message in get_messages(response.wsgi_request)]
        self.client.cookies.pop("messages", None)
        return lines

    def refused(self, path, data=None):
        """POST to `path`, follow the redirect to Billing, and return (response, sentence, record): the page, the one line it shows
        above the heading, and the one `billing: dashboard refusal` record the request logged through the drop_billing logger."""
        with self.assertLogs("drop_billing", level="WARNING") as captured:
            response = self.client.post(path, data or {}, follow=True)
        self.assertEqual(response.redirect_chain, [(self.billing, 302)], f"{VIEWS}: a refusal goes back to Billing, not to a 400 or a 500")
        records = [record for record in captured.records if LOGGED.match(record.getMessage())]
        self.assertEqual(len(records), 1, f"{VIEWS}: a refusal logs one 'billing: dashboard refusal ref=' line through the drop_billing logger")
        lines = self.said(response)
        self.assertEqual(len(lines), 1, f"{VIEWS}: and leaves one line for Billing")
        return response, lines[0], records[0]

    def assertFixed(self, sentence, fixed, record, level, why):
        """A refusal the page explains: the fixed sentence as it is, no reference, and a log line at `level`."""
        self.assertEqual(sentence, fixed, f"{VIEWS}: {why}")
        self.assertIsNone(REFERENCE.search(sentence), f"{VIEWS}: a sentence that says why needs no reference")
        self.assertEqual(record.levelno, level, f"backend/dashboard/billing_page.py: refusal() logs {logging.getLevelName(level)} for this")

    def assertReferenced(self, response, sentence, fixed, record, secret):
        """A refusal the page cannot explain: `fixed`, then 'Reference: XXXXXX'; the log line carries that reference and `secret` (what
        Stripe said), at ERROR; and neither the sentence nor the page holds `secret` or any word of the operator."""
        match = REFERENCE.search(sentence)
        self.assertIsNotNone(match, f"{VIEWS}: the sentence ends with 'Reference: ' and six capitals or digits, got {sentence!r}")
        self.assertEqual(sentence, f"{fixed} Reference: {match.group(1)}", f"{VIEWS}: the fixed sentence, then the reference")
        logged = record.getMessage()
        self.assertEqual(LOGGED.match(logged).group(1), match.group(1), "backend/dashboard/billing_page.py: the reference on the page is the one in the log")
        self.assertEqual(record.levelno, logging.ERROR, "backend/dashboard/billing_page.py: refusal() logs ERROR for a failure the page cannot explain")
        if secret:
            self.assertIn(secret, logged, "backend/dashboard/billing_page.py: the log line holds what Stripe said")
        html = response.content.decode()
        text = visible_text(html)
        self.assertIn(sentence, text, f"{PAGE}: the sentence is on the page")
        for word in OPERATOR_WORDS + ((secret,) if secret else ()):
            self.assertNotIn(word, text, f"{VIEWS}: the page must not show {word!r}; it goes to the log")
        if secret:
            self.assertNotIn(secret, html, f"{VIEWS}: Stripe's message is not in the page at all")

    def subscribe(self, plan="team", status="active"):
        """The workspace pays for `plan`; Stripe's list says the same."""
        self.set_billing(plan, customer="cus_A", sub_id="sub_A", status=status)
        return self.patch_stripe("list", return_value=sub_list(make_sub("sub_A", status, f"price_{plan}")))

    def lapse(self, status):
        """A workspace that fell to free while the mirror still names the subscription's status."""
        self.set_billing("free", customer="cus_A")
        Subscription.objects.update_or_create(
            workspace=self.ws,
            defaults={"stripe_customer_id": "cus_A", "stripe_subscription_id": "sub_A", "status": status})

    def no_stripe(self):
        """Every Stripe call these pages could make, patched; assertNoStripe says none was made."""
        return {key: self.patch_stripe(key) for key in ("list", "modify", "customer", "session", "portal", "void", "retrieve_customer")}

    def assertNoStripe(self, calls, message):
        for key, patched in calls.items():
            self.assertFalse(patched.called, f"{message}: stripe {key} was called")

    def assertSentTo(self, response, location, message):
        self.assertEqual((response.status_code, response.get("Location")), (302, location), message)

    def pending(self, **changes):
        """An unpaid switch in the session, as billing_page.remember_pending writes it, with these fields changed."""
        session = self.client.session
        session[billing_page.PENDING_KEY] = {"plan": "scale", "invoice_url": INVOICE, "at": int(time.time()), **changes}
        session.save()

    def stripe_ready(self, url=STRIPE_URL):
        """Stripe, as it answers a checkout for a workspace with no customer yet: (customer, list, session)."""
        customer = self.patch_stripe("customer", return_value={"id": "cus_new"})
        lister = self.patch_stripe("list", return_value=sub_list())
        session = self.patch_stripe("session", return_value={"id": "cs_test_1", "url": url})
        return customer, lister, session

    def go_over(self, keys=0, storage=False, ttl=False):
        """The free plan's workspace over the limits asked for (the way OverLimitTests do it)."""
        caps = PLANS["free"]
        for index in range(keys):
            APIKey.create_key(self.ws, f"key {index}")
        if storage or ttl:
            Artifact.objects.create(
                workspace=self.ws, filename="big.bin",
                size_bytes=(caps["storage_gb"] + 1) * 1024**3 if storage else 1,
                expires_at=timezone.now() + timedelta(days=caps["ttl_days"] + 300 if ttl else 1))


class BillingPageModuleTests(SimpleTestCase):
    """backend/dashboard/billing_page.py: what is not HTTP."""
    longMessage = False
    FILE = "backend/dashboard/billing_page.py"

    def test_the_plans_for_sale_are_the_plans_that_have_a_price(self):
        self.assertEqual(billing_page.paid_plans(), ["team", "scale"], f"{self.FILE}: paid_plans() lists the plans of plans.py that have a price")
        with mock.patch.dict(PLANS, {"pro": {**PLANS["scale"], "price_usd": 30}}):
            self.assertEqual(billing_page.paid_plans(), ["team", "scale", "pro"], f"{self.FILE}: a plan added to plans.py is for sale at once")

    def test_a_plan_is_named_the_way_the_plans_chapter_names_it(self):
        self.assertEqual([billing_page.plan_name(slug) for slug in PLANS], ["Free", "Team", "Scale"], f"{self.FILE}: plan_name() capitalises the slug")

    def test_only_an_https_address_is_followed(self):
        good = "https://checkout.stripe.com/c/pay/cs_1"
        self.assertEqual(billing_page.https_only(good), good, f"{self.FILE}: https_only() keeps an https address")
        for bad in ("http://checkout.stripe.com/x", "javascript:alert(1)", "//evil.example/x", "HTTPS://x", "", None, 7, ["https://x"]):
            with self.subTest(url=bad):
                self.assertIsNone(billing_page.https_only(bad), f"{self.FILE}: https_only() gives None for anything that does not start with https://")
```
